commits.pr_title: [Perf][Frontend] Validate plain embedding inputs before the full union
commits.pr_body:
## Overview

`EmbeddingRequest` is a five-member pydantic union with no discriminator, so every `/v1/embeddings` body is validated against all five. The chat-input members (#45173) check each input item against every chat message type, so a 256×64 token-id batch spends ~66 ms in validation on the API server's event loop. This tries `EmbeddingCompletionRequest` first when `input` is not chat-shaped and the body has no chat-only field, and otherwise (or on any error) falls back to the original union.

## Claims

- Validation of plain inputs: 256×64 token ids ~66 ms → 0.28 ms, 256 strings 818 → 44 µs, 1 string 20 → 4.8 µs.
- Parsed requests, `errors()` and HTTP 400 bodies are unchanged; chat bodies take the original path (+~0.4 µs for the check).
- Reach: `/v1/embeddings` (and `run_batch`) with string or token-id input. The Rust frontend has no embeddings route.

## Validation

A/B, 15 alternated rounds, fresh process per run, validation through the route's FastAPI body field; macOS arm64, Python 3.12.7, pydantic 2.14.1:

| body | main | PR |
|---|---|---|
| 256×64 token ids | 65.6 ms | 0.28 ms |
| 32×512 token ids | 64.9 ms | 0.15 ms |
| 256 strings | 818 µs | 44 µs |
| 1 chat conversation | 32.3 µs | 32.7 µs |
| ScoreRequest (control) | 15.6 µs | 15.7 µs |

<details>
<summary>Reproduce</summary>

```python
import time
from pydantic import TypeAdapter
from vllm.entrypoints.pooling.embed.protocol import EmbeddingRequest

ta = TypeAdapter(EmbeddingRequest)
body = {"model": "m", "input": [list(range(64)) for _ in range(256)]}
ta.validate_python(body)
t = time.perf_counter()
for _ in range(20):
    ta.validate_python(body)
print(f"{(time.perf_counter() - t) / 20 * 1e3:.2f} ms")  # main 68.3, PR 0.26
```
</details>

Identity vs main: 55 valid bodies (every input shape and option, chat/batched/chat-as-input variants, both `input` and `messages`) parse to the same class and `model_dump()` over HTTP and through `run_batch`; 35 invalid bodies give the same status and errors.

```
pytest tests/entrypoints/pooling/embed/test_io_processor.py
# 64 passed
```

The new tests compare against the plain union for 11 valid and 4 invalid bodies; the invalid set fails if the chat-only-field check is removed. Evals: N/A, model inputs are unchanged. End-to-end server latency was not measured; numbers are the validation step only.

Not a duplicate: no open or closed PR touches this union (`EmbeddingRequest`, `embeddings discriminator`, `pooling protocol union`).

## Details

Only the completion member can accept a non-chat `input` without `messages`, so when it validates, the result matches the union. Bodies with a chat-only field (`_CHAT_ONLY_FIELDS`, derived from `EmbeddingChatRequest.model_fields`) skip the fast path, because chat-member validators can reject them with a non-`ValidationError` (e.g. `continue_final_message` + `add_generation_prompt`). A `WrapValidator` is used instead of a `Discriminator`, which would change error `loc`s and the OpenAPI schema (`anyOf` → `oneOf`). Only cosmetic difference: `ValidationError.title` names the wrapper, visible in the first line of `run_batch` error strings.

AI assistance (Claude Opus 5.5) was used to find this target, draft the patch, and build the benchmark and identity check. I reviewed every line, re-ran the tests, and benchmarks above myself, and can answer for the change and where the perf wins come from.

commits.pr_title: [Model] Muse Glimmer: reuse in-tree RMSNorm / GemmaRMSNorm
commits.pr_body:
## Overview

Replace the model-local `MuseGlimmerRMSNorm` (added in #51655) with the existing `RMSNorm` and `GemmaRMSNorm` CustomOps. The output is bit-identical in bf16.

## Claims

- Removes the model-local `MuseGlimmerRMSNorm` class. All norms in the model now use the shared CustomOps, so they get are enabled for the OOT-platform swapping.
- No numerical change: each replacement matches the old class bit-for-bit in bf16.
- No checkpoint or weight-loading change: parameter names and shapes are unchanged.

## Validation

Old class vs replacement, bf16, A100, x = 257×5120, both `forward_native` and `forward_cuda`:

| Norm (old config) | Replacement | Result |
|---|---|---|
| `with_scale=False` (`qk_norm`, `embed_norm`, `perception_emb_norm`) | `RMSNorm(dim, has_weight=False)` | bit-exact |
| `weight_offset=1` (4 sandwich norms) | `GemmaRMSNorm(dim)` | bit-exact |
| final `norm` | `RMSNorm(dim, dtype=torch.float32)` | bit-exact |

```bash
.venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/models/test_initialization.py \
    -k "MuseGlimmerForCausalLM or MuseGlimmerForConditionalGeneration" -v
# 2 passed
```

gsm8k on `meta-models/Muse-Glimmer-30B` (BF16, TP=2 on 2×A100-80GB, `--model-impl vllm`, 5-shot, 1319 questions, greedy, max 256 tokens):

| | Accuracy | Correct | Invalid | Throughput (tok/s) |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| main (`e318ac0979`) | 0.9181 | 1211 / 1319 | 1 | 1911 |
| this PR | 0.9189 | 1212 / 1319 | 0 | 1930 |

The 1-question delta is batching noise; the norms themselves are bit-exact.

```bash
vllm serve meta-models/Muse-Glimmer-30B --model-impl vllm --dtype bfloat16 \
    --tensor-parallel-size 2 --max-model-len 4096 \
    --limit-mm-per-prompt '{"image": 0, "video": 0}'
python tests/evals/gsm8k/gsm8k_eval.py --num-shots 5 --num-questions 1319
```

## Details

The old class covered three cases, each of which already exists in-tree:

- **No weight:** `norm(x.float()).type_as(x)` is `RMSNorm(has_weight=False)`.
- **`(1 + w)` sandwich norms:** these are HF's `MuseGlimmerTextCenteredRMSNorm`, a copy of Gemma's norm, so `GemmaRMSNorm` matches.
- **Final norm:** HF computes `(norm(x.float()) * w.float()).type_as(x)`. The in-tree op multiplies in the weight's dtype, so the weight is kept in fp32 to match HF's single cast. The fp32 weight survives the bf16 default dtype at init and `default_weight_loader`. The trade-off is that the fused `vllm_c` kernel requires matching weight/input dtypes, so this one norm (once per forward) takes the native PyTorch path instead.

Not in scope: Gemma2-style fused residual-add in the decoder layer, which would change `forward`.

No open PR touches this: searched open PRs for `MuseGlimmerRMSNorm`, `MuseGlimmer RMSNorm` and `muse_glimmer norm`.

cc @xianbaoqian @jeejeelee @zixi-qi @TheEpicDolphin (authors of #51655)

commits.pr_title: [Rust Frontend][gRPC] Separate liveness from inference readiness
commits.pr_body:
## Update: stacked on #64265, readiness reported by the engines

**Stacked on #64265** (`[Rust Frontend] Run utility calls to completion when the caller is cancelled`). The base branch `bz/rust-uncancellable-utility` mirrors #64265's head; this PR will be retargeted to `main` once #64265 merges. Its three commits:

- f2ed5490bc (Julien): this PR's net change, squashed from the previous history (last head 21feaf4a8e, which also merged main).
- c7c67d866c: holds the readiness guard until the engines reply.
- 5ac1ff2fe7: withdraws readiness before the gRPC listener stops, including when the server is aborted.

This revision keeps the gRPC service mapping and changes how the frontend learns the engine state. The original revision inferred it in the client from the results of the control calls it sent (`client/availability.rs`: per-call facts, `resolve`, epochs, and a confirm loop asking `is_sleeping` plus a worker RPC). EngineCore already owns that state, so it now reports it:

- `EngineCore.is_inference_ready()` (Python, 8 lines): not paused (including for a checkpoint) or asleep, and no worker reports `has_incomplete_weight_update()`.
- The client (`client/readiness.rs`) withdraws readiness before a call that stops serving is sent (pause, sleep, checkpoint prepare, start weight update), and rechecks after every control call ends by asking the engines `is_inference_ready`. An epoch discards answers that predate a call, so readiness becomes `SERVING` only from an engine answer. The public `collective_rpc` also rechecks, which covers weight updates and the dev-mode `/collective_rpc` route.
- A control call passes its readiness guard to `call_utility`, whose task (from #64265) holds it until the engines reply. A caller cancelled after sending a pause, for example by a client disconnecting from `/pause`, therefore cannot recheck before the engines have handled the pause.
- The client asks only while someone subscribes (the gRPC server), so HTTP-only deployments add no worker RPC after control calls.
- With sleep mode, the client asks once at connect: only such engines can start prepared for a checkpoint (`--checkpoint-prepare-on-startup`), and an engine without the utility fails startup with an error naming it.
- gRPC wiring: `EngineHealth` groups the client's liveness and readiness watches, and `HealthMonitor` registers the services before the listener accepts connections and then follows the watches.
- Shutdown order: `HealthMonitor::serve` runs the gRPC server, and both the signal that stops its listener and the forced abort (immediate with the default `--shutdown-timeout 0`) wait until every service except `liveness` reports `NOT_SERVING`. A `Health/Watch` subscriber therefore receives the withdrawal before its connection closes. A `Check` on a new connection after shutdown starts gets `NOT_SERVING`, an unknown service, or a refused connection; probes treat all three as not ready. `lib.rs` and the gRPC test server share this wiring.
- `finish_weight_update` clears the worker's incomplete-update flag only after the draft model's quantized LM heads are restored, so a failed restore keeps readiness withdrawn.

The service mapping is the same as in the original revision:

| Service | Reports `NOT_SERVING` when |
| --- | --- |
| `liveness` | The engine has failed. |
| `readiness` and `vllm.Inference` | The engines report not ready, a call that stops serving is in flight, the engine has failed, or shutdown has started. |
| `vllm.Control` and `""` | The engine has failed or shutdown has started. |

`readiness` always equals `vllm.Inference`; both are kept. Kubernetes probes and the Dynamo sidecar use `liveness` and `readiness` (ai-dynamo/dynamo#14897), while `vllm.Inference` and `vllm.Control` remain the per-service statuses.

Validation of this revision:
- `cargo nextest run -p vllm-server -p vllm-engine-core-client -p vllm-mock-engine`: 701 passed. `cargo clippy --workspace --tests --examples -- -D warnings`, `cargo fmt --check`, and `pre-commit` passed.
- New tests: unit tests for the readiness state (an answer that predates a call is discarded, an in-flight withdrawal hides answers, no asks without subscribers); scripted-engine client tests (pause and resume, weight update, starting prepared with sleep mode, and a pause whose caller is cancelled must not be rechecked before the engine replies); gRPC tests (a pause withdraws only `readiness` and `vllm.Inference`, orderly shutdown closes the `liveness` watch without `NOT_SERVING`, engine failure fails all five services); a worker test where a failed draft finish keeps the weights incomplete; `HealthMonitor` tests where the listener stop and a forced abort both find readiness already withdrawn (300 consecutive runs). Each fails when its fix is reverted.
- `pytest tests/v1/worker/test_gpu_worker_weight_transfer.py`: passes; one existing test needs a visible GPU and was not run.
- Live GPU runs: the table below replays the original revision's table on c7c67d866c. On 5ac1ff2fe7, three SIGTERM runs repeated the SIGTERM row: every watch except `liveness` received `NOT_SERVING` within 3 ms and then closed.

Live runs of c7c67d866c on one GB200 GPU with `Qwen/Qwen3-0.6B`, `--enable-sleep-mode --weight-transfer-config '{"backend":"ipc"}'`, and `VLLM_SERVER_DEV_MODE=1`. Control steps use the `vllm.Control` RPCs, except the HTTP checkpoint and draft routes. Each check opens a new connection, as kubelet does, and `Health/Watch` streams on the services record every transition.

| Step | `readiness`, `vllm.Inference` | `liveness`, `vllm.Control`, `""` |
| --- | --- | --- |
| After startup, then a completion | SERVING | SERVING |
| `PauseGeneration` in `abort`, `wait`, and `keep` modes | NOT_SERVING | SERVING |
| `ResumeGeneration` after each, then a completion | SERVING | SERVING |
| `Sleep(level=1)`, then `WakeUp(tags=["weights"])` | NOT_SERVING | SERVING |
| Full `WakeUp`, then a completion | SERVING | SERVING |
| `keep` pause held 180 s, checked every 10 s | NOT_SERVING throughout, no transition on the watch | `liveness` SERVING throughout |
| Resume after the long pause | SERVING, same `instance_id` | SERVING |
| `POST /start_draft_weight_update` without a draft model (the workers refuse), then a completion | NOT_SERVING for 6 ms, then SERVING | SERVING |
| `StartWeightUpdate` | NOT_SERVING | SERVING |
| `FinishWeightUpdate`, then a completion | SERVING | SERVING |
| `StartWeightUpdate`, then `UpdateWeights` with `update_info_json` set to `{}` (fails) | NOT_SERVING | SERVING |
| `FinishWeightUpdate` after the failed load (fails) | NOT_SERVING, no SERVING on the watch since the start | SERVING |
| New `StartWeightUpdate` and `FinishWeightUpdate`, then a completion | SERVING | SERVING |
| `POST /checkpoint/prepare`, until `/checkpoint/status` returns 200 | NOT_SERVING | SERVING |
| `POST /checkpoint/restore`, then a completion | SERVING | SERVING |
| Started with `--checkpoint-prepare-on-startup` | NOT_SERVING | SERVING |
| `POST /checkpoint/restore`, then a completion | SERVING | SERVING |
| `PauseGeneration(wait)` during a 3000-token request, with a 0.5 s deadline that cancels the call; checked after the 6 s drain | NOT_SERVING, no SERVING on the watch; `IsPaused` true | SERVING |
| `ResumeGeneration`, then a completion | SERVING | SERVING |
| Dev-mode `POST /collective_rpc` with `start_weight_update` | NOT_SERVING | SERVING |
| `POST /collective_rpc` with `finish_weight_update`, then a completion | SERVING | SERVING |
| SIGTERM | Watch receives NOT_SERVING, then closes | `liveness` watch closes without NOT_SERVING; listener closed 4 ms later |
| `kill -9` of the EngineCore process | Watch receives NOT_SERVING, then closes | `liveness` watch closes without NOT_SERVING; `vllm-rs` exits with an error |

- The cancelled pause is a smoke test: the pause reaches the engine long before the deadline, so it also passes without #64265. The race it guards against, a recheck overtaking the pause, is covered by `cancelled_pause_rechecks_only_after_the_engine_replies`.
- `kill -9`: the engine failure path sets `liveness` last, and the server aborts the gRPC listener at the same time, so the `liveness` watch closed before receiving NOT_SERVING. This is the race described under the original revision's `kill -9` row; probes treat a closed connection as a failure.

AI assistance (Claude) was used for this revision.

---

## Original description (previous revision)

## Overview

The Rust frontend's gRPC health service reports the same status for every service name, so Kubernetes and sidecars cannot tell an engine paused for an RL weight update from one that needs a restart. This adds two health services: `liveness`, which fails only when the engine fails, and `readiness`, which also fails while the engine is paused (including for a process checkpoint) or asleep, or while a weight update has not finished successfully. `vllm.Inference` now reports the same status as `readiness`; `vllm.Control`, `""`, and the protobufs are unchanged. Motivation: [ai-dynamo/dynamo#14897](https://github.com/ai-dynamo/dynamo/issues/14897).

**Size: about 325 lines of non-test Rust and 8 lines of Python** (+336/−34, not counting tests, comments, blank lines, reindentation, or the 39 lines moved unchanged onto `ClientInner`). The logic is four pieces:

- the engine-state tracker in `client/availability.rs`, about 170 lines:
  - two facts (every engine is scheduling; every worker's weights are complete) and the rule that readiness is SERVING when both allow serving, keeping its last value while one is being confirmed;
  - a guard each control call holds, which withdraws readiness before a pause or update start is sent and records the fact the call's result settles;
  - a background loop that runs while either fact is unknown (after a resume, a weight-update finish, a failed or cancelled call, or overlapping calls). It asks the engines `is_sleeping` and the workers `has_incomplete_weight_update`, asks again if another control call made the answer stale, and retries a failed attempt every second.
- the wiring in `client.rs` and `client/imp.rs`, about 90 lines:
  - each pause, sleep, resume, wake-up, weight-update and checkpoint method takes the guard;
  - `ClientInner` keeps the engine IDs and client index, so the loop can call the engines;
  - `subscribe_availability`, the loop's task, and one `is_sleeping` call at connect for sleep-mode engines, which may start prepared for a checkpoint.
- the gRPC mapping in `grpc/health.rs` and `lib.rs`, about 70 lines:
  - register `liveness`, and register `readiness` and `vllm.Inference` with the current availability;
  - drive `readiness` and `vllm.Inference` from the tracker;
  - on shutdown, publish NOT_SERVING before the listener stops accepting connections.
- the worker method `has_incomplete_weight_update()` in `gpu_worker.py` and `worker_base.py`, 8 lines: tracked per target (base or draft model), set once an update starts, and cleared by that target's successful finish. Because of the second target, a successful finish asks the workers rather than assuming the weights are complete.

Moving the existing `call_utility` and `collective_rpc` fan-out onto `ClientInner` changes no behavior. The rest of the +1119/−162 diff is:
- tests (+575/−63): 7 new tests (5 Rust, 2 Python), the two existing health tests and the existing full-wake-up test extended, gRPC test setup that passes the tracker, and the new worker attribute in hand-built test workers;
- docs (+43 in `docs/deployment/k8s.md` and `rust/README.md`);
- doc comments.

## Claims

- `liveness` reports `NOT_SERVING` only after an engine failure. Pause, sleep, checkpoint prepare, weight updates, and orderly shutdown do not affect it until the listener closes.
- `readiness` and `vllm.Inference` report `NOT_SERVING` in these cases:
  - while a pause, sleep (including a partial wake-up), or process-checkpoint prepare sent through this frontend's HTTP or gRPC control APIs is in effect;
  - while an engine started with `--checkpoint-prepare-on-startup` is not yet restored;
  - from the start of a weight update until one finishes successfully, including after a failed load;
  - on engine failure or shutdown. On shutdown they are withdrawn before the listener stops accepting connections. With the default `--shutdown-timeout 0`, the gRPC server is aborted without a grace period, so a Watch can see its connection close before it receives `NOT_SERVING`; probes treat both as not ready.
- Kubernetes probes: startup and liveness use `liveness`, readiness uses `readiness`, as documented in `docs/deployment/k8s.md`. A liveness probe that names `vllm.Inference` now fails while the engine stays paused, so it should move to `liveness`. Likewise, a client that waits for `vllm.Inference` to be SERVING before it connects now waits while the engine is paused. Dynamo's vLLM sidecar does this at startup (`lib/sidecar/vllm/src/engine.rs`). To connect to a paused engine, wait on `vllm.Control`, which reports SERVING while paused in every version; earlier versions do not have `liveness`.

## Validation

Live runs on 1x RTX 6000 Ada with this branch, polling `grpc.health.v1.Health/Check` every 0.5 s on a new connection, as kubelet does:

```bash
VLLM_USE_FLASHINFER_SAMPLER=0 vllm-rs serve Qwen/Qwen3-0.6B --grpc-port 50051 -- --enable-sleep-mode
```

The weight-update rows add `--weight-transfer-config '{"backend":"ipc"}'` and `VLLM_SERVER_DEV_MODE=1`. The failed load sends `UpdateWeights` with `update_info_json` set to `{}`. The last checkpoint rows add `--checkpoint-prepare-on-startup`.

| Step | `readiness`, `vllm.Inference` | `liveness`, `vllm.Control`, `""` |
| --- | --- | --- |
| After startup, then a completion | SERVING | SERVING |
| `PauseGeneration` in `abort`, `wait`, and `keep` modes | NOT_SERVING | SERVING |
| `ResumeGeneration` after each, then a completion | SERVING | SERVING |
| `Sleep(level=1)`, then `WakeUp(tags=["weights"])` | NOT_SERVING | SERVING |
| Full `WakeUp`, then a completion | SERVING | SERVING |
| `keep` pause held 180 s, checked every 10 s | NOT_SERVING throughout | `liveness` SERVING throughout |
| Resume after the long pause | SERVING, same `instance_id` | SERVING |
| `POST /start_draft_weight_update` without a draft model (the workers refuse), then a completion | NOT_SERVING for 4 ms, then SERVING | SERVING |
| `StartWeightUpdate` | NOT_SERVING | SERVING |
| `FinishWeightUpdate`, then a completion | SERVING | SERVING |
| `StartWeightUpdate`, then a failed `UpdateWeights` | NOT_SERVING | SERVING |
| `FinishWeightUpdate` after the failed load (fails) | NOT_SERVING | SERVING |
| New `StartWeightUpdate` and `FinishWeightUpdate`, then a completion | SERVING | SERVING |
| `POST /checkpoint/prepare`, until `/checkpoint/status` returns 200 | NOT_SERVING | SERVING |
| `POST /checkpoint/restore`, then a completion | SERVING | SERVING |
| Started with `--checkpoint-prepare-on-startup` | NOT_SERVING | SERVING |
| `POST /checkpoint/restore`, then a completion | SERVING | SERVING |
| SIGTERM | Watch receives NOT_SERVING, then closes | `liveness` watch closes without NOT_SERVING; listener closed by the next check, under 0.4 s later |
| `kill -9` of the EngineCore process | Watch receives NOT_SERVING then closes, or the connection drops first | Listener closes; `vllm-rs` exits with an error |

Provenance:
- All rows except the 180 s pause and `kill -9` rows ran on 5073411766. They also cover the head, d42905b98a, which changes only tests and docs.
- The 180 s pause rows ran on 3c2f1d1525.
- With the worker change reverted, the refused draft start left `readiness` NOT_SERVING.
- The `kill -9` row is timing-dependent on both sides of this change: the watch received NOT_SERVING before the connection dropped in 5 of 8 runs on a build of this head without its last two fixes (the finish confirmation and the repeated-status filter), and in 5 of 7 runs on 8ae979f973. When the managed engine exits, the server shuts down with no grace period, so aborting the gRPC server races the health monitor's update.

`VLLM_USE_FLASHINFER_SAMPLER=0` only works around the test machine's CUDA 11.5 `nvcc`.

Unit tests:
- `cargo nextest run -p vllm-server -p vllm-engine-core-client -p vllm-mock-engine` passed (686, with a short `TMPDIR` for the two Unix-socket listener tests), as did `cargo clippy --tests -- -D warnings`, `cargo fmt --check`, and `pre-commit`.
- The availability and health tests passed 20 consecutive runs.
- `pytest tests/v1/worker/test_gpu_worker_weight_transfer.py` passed (17), and `pytest tests/v1/worker/test_gpu_draft_lm_head.py -k draft_weight_update` passed on the GPU (3).
- The new tests use the scripted mock engine or a stub weight-transfer engine. Each fails when its fix is reverted: the re-ask after a stale answer, the retry, the refusal branch of checkpoint prepare, setting the worker flag before the draft-model check, a single flag shared by base and draft, and a finish that does not clear the flag.

Not run:
- a weight transfer from a real trainer;
- a draft-model weight update;
- worker failure with TP > 1;
- probes in a Kubernetes cluster.

No model evaluation: generated tokens are unaffected.

## Details

The worker reports `has_incomplete_weight_update` rather than whether an update session is active because a failed `update_weights` ends the session without restoring the weights, so generation fails until a later update finishes.

Known limitations:
- Pauses that bypass these client methods, such as the dev-mode `/collective_rpc` route, are not observed.
- A full wake-up after a level-2 sleep reports SERVING before the weights are reloaded. The documented order (wake `weights`, reload, then wake `kv_cache`) keeps readiness down until the weights are back.
- A failed process checkpoint leaves the engine paused, with no way to restore. `readiness` stays `NOT_SERVING` and `liveness` stays `SERVING`, so whatever drives the checkpoint must restart the pod when `/checkpoint/status` reports the failure.

The frontend infers engine state from the results of the calls it sends and asks the engines when a result is not conclusive. An engine-reported readiness state, as proposed in [#60505](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/60505), could replace these confirmations.

No open or merged PR splits Rust gRPC liveness from readiness (checked 2026-10-26). [#60505](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/60505) and [#59179](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/59179) add Python HTTP readiness endpoints; [#56886](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/56886) (draft) adds a gRPC shutdown grace period.

AI assistance (Claude) was used to write and review this change.

commits.pr_body:
## Overview

commits.pr_title: [Model Loader] One post-load hook signature; the loader runs every module's hook
commits.pr_body:
## Purpose

This PR now carries a follow-up to #64357. The earlier revision ran the model-level hook on every load and reload; that landed in reworked form as #64357. Part of RFC #54477.

#64357 made `finalize_model_weights(model)` run once after every full load and reload, but it calls only the **root model's** `process_weights_after_loading`. Module-level hooks still had two signatures:

| module | signature | who called it |
|---|---|---|
| attention layers (`Attention`, `MLAAttention`, `MMEncoderAttention`, Kimi-K3 MLA / KDA, DeepSeek-V4 CPU attention) | `(act_dtype)` | loader, attention pass |
| root model | `()` | `finalize_model_weights` |
| any other module (VL language models, HY-V4 inner model, Dots3 vision MoE FFN, Kimi-K3 AMD MLA wrapper) | `()` | **its parent, by hand** |

So parents forwarded the hook to their submodules by hand: VL wrappers to `language_model`, Kimi-K3 AMD through a `modules()` loop, Dots3 to `visual` and then to each `block.mlp`, and so on. When a parent forgot to forward, the submodule was never processed, with no error. The loader also carried `TODO(lucas): see if there is a way to unify the signatures`.

## Changes

1. **One signature.** Attention layers record `self.act_dtype` at init and take no argument. This is the default dtype the loader sets from `model_config.dtype` while building the model, which is the same value the loader used to pass. Backend impls (`AttentionImpl.process_weights_after_loading(act_dtype)`) are unchanged.
2. **One dispatcher.** After the quant-method pass and the attention pass, `finalize_model_weights` runs the hook of every module, each module after all of its submodules (depth-first; a submodule shared by several parents runs once, before all of them). It skips quant methods (some are `CustomOp` modules whose hook takes `layer`), does not enter quantized layers (their submodules, such as compressed-tensors Hadamard transforms, belong to the quant method and are processed in the per-layer pass), and skips attention layers, which have already run. The stages stay as they are: per-layer quant pass → attention pass → module hooks; later passes may read what earlier ones produced (e.g. MLA absorbs `kv_b_proj` through its transforms in the attention pass).
3. **No hand forwarding.** These are deleted:
   - the DeepSeek-V4 / V4.1 (AMD, NVIDIA) VL wrapper and Kimi-K3 AMD wrapper forwards to `language_model`;
   - the HY-V4 AMD forward to `self.model`;
   - the Dots3 forwards to `visual` and to the `block.mlp` loop;
   - the Kimi-K3 AMD MLA-wrapper loop.

### Behavior

- **Ordering.** As before, all attention layers run before any module hook, and a module's hook runs after its submodules', which is what the deleted forwards guaranteed. Siblings run in registration order. No hook reads a sibling's derived state.
- **No hook runs for the first time, and none runs twice.** I enumerated every class with a no-argument `process_weights_after_loading` (AST scan of `vllm/`). Each one was already reached, either as a root model or through one of the forwards deleted above.
- **Layerwise reload and the sparse NCCL engine** both go through `finalize_model_weights`, so they get the same dispatch.

## Test Plan

- **New test.** `test_finalize_runs_every_module_hook_after_its_submodules` (`tests/model_executor/model_loader/test_reload.py`) checks that each module runs exactly once (including one shared by two parents), after its submodules, with quant-method modules, quantized layers' submodules and attention layers skipped. `test_attention_post_load_reads_normalized_transform` runs the real loader `process_weights_after_loading` with a real `CompressedTensorsLinearTransformMethod` + `HadamardTransform` and checks that the attention pass sees the transform already normalized, and normalized once.
- **Updated tests.**
  - The fake attention layers in `test_reload.py`, plus `test_mla_backends`, `test_vit_fp8_scaling` and `test_mla_attn_quant_fusion`, now call the hook without an argument.
  - `test_deepseek_v4_vl` now goes through `finalize_model_weights`.
  - `test_root_model_builds_the_fold` asserted the old forward-by-hand contract, so it is deleted.
- **End to end.** GSM8K before and after weight updates, on GB300.

## Test Result

All runs are on GB300, using the same image and seed, against plain main at `7fc467825d`, the PR's base.

**GSM8K.** Each run measures GSM8K at cold start, then again after 3 full-checkpoint direct reloads (`VLLM_RELOAD_MODE=direct`).

| model | what it exercises | main: cold → after reload | PR: cold → after reload |
|---|---|---|---|
| Qwen3-8B | `Attention` reads `act_dtype` from init | 0.895 → 0.895 | 0.895 → 0.895 |
| DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash (TP2) | VL wrapper no longer forwards to `language_model` | 0.899 → 0.898 | 0.900 → 0.907 |
| gpt-oss-20b | attention sinks, MXFP4 MoE quant method is a `CustomOp` | 0.438 → 0.023 | 0.444 → 0.022 |

Cold start matches main within noise for all three models. gpt-oss-20b also collapses after a direct reload on plain main; that is a separate issue, fixed in #64692, and unchanged by this PR.

**Unit tests.** 332 passed, 21 failed, 41 skipped. The two new tests pass, and so do the updated tests. `test_attention_post_load_reads_normalized_transform` fails on the previous head of this PR (`fb3b81ad63`, attention saw `1.0` instead of `0.5`), which is the regression a review caught: that head ran Hadamard transforms in the module pass, after MLA had already absorbed `kv_b_proj`. None of the 21 failures comes from this PR:
- **7 DeepSeek-V3 reload tests** (`test_reload_weights` / `test_online_quantize_reload` with DeepSeek-V3-debug, and `test_kv_scale_reload`). They fail the same way on plain main.
- **14 GLM5-next KDA / sequence-parallel tests.** They failed only in the full batch run. Rerun on their own, they pass on both main and this PR.

commits.pr_title: [Bugfix][Kernel] Only set PDL launch attr for MoE top-k gating on SM90+
commits.pr_body:
## Overview

Fixes #65055. Since #59737, `topkGating` is launched with the PDL attribute on every CUDA arch. Pre-SM90 GPUs cannot use PDL, but stream capture still records the attribute as a programmatic edge in the CUDA graph, and replaying those graphs is slower. This PR sets the attribute only when the device is SM90+. SM90+ keeps the #59737 behaviour; older GPUs launch without the attribute, which measured the same as the v0.32 `<<<>>>` launch. The standalone effect was measured on sm80, sm86 and sm89; end-to-end numbers are A100 only.

## Claims

- 4× A100, TP4 + EP + MTP (our deployment config, private NVFP4 checkpoint of Qwen3.8-Flash-Next; setup below): per-request decode is 6.5–13.6% faster in 17 of 18 prompt × concurrency (1–16) cells, and 2.1% in the 18th. At concurrency 16: prose 74.3 → 80.1 and code 88.7 → 94.8 tok/s, close to the last commit before #59737 (3b05805d4: 81.5 and 95.3, one run).
- Standalone CUDA (no vLLM): the attribute adds one programmatic edge per launch and 0.6–1.1 µs of graph replay per edge on A100 (sm80), RTX A4000 (sm86) and RTX 4090 (sm89), in every round; without the attribute `cudaLaunchKernelEx` matches `<<<>>>`.
- 1× A100, CUDA graph replay of a router GEMM → `topk_softmax` chain: 6.9–9.0% faster for Qwen3.8-Flash-Next, Qwen3-30B-A3B and OLMoE shapes at 1/16/48 tokens, in every round against a no-change rebuild.
- 1× A100 end to end, `vllm bench latency`: batch 1 is 0.7% faster for OLMoE-1B-7B (every round vs a no-change rebuild, 2 of 3 rounds vs the shipped build) and 1.2% faster for Qwen3-30B-A3B-GPTQ-Int4 (every round). Batch 16 is within noise for both.
- No accuracy change: GSM8K 5-shot on Qwen3-30B-A3B-GPTQ-Int4 is 85.90% (base) vs 86.13% (fix). The kernel body is identical.
- SM90+ is unchanged by construction (the same attribute is set as before); not measured.

## Validation

Hardware: A100-PCIE-40GB, driver 590.48.01, CUDA 13.0, torch 2.14.0+cu130, vLLM v0.33.0 (4ba787ec9). `base` = the v0.33.0 `_moe_C` as shipped. `rebuilt` = the same source built with the same toolchain, no change. `fix` = `rebuilt` + this diff. Builds are `_moe_C` only, for sm80, overlaid on the v0.33.0 install. The diff applies unchanged to main (the file is identical).

**Tests**

- `pytest tests/kernels/moe/test_fused_topk.py` on A100: base 864 passed, fix 864 passed.
- GSM8K 5-shot, 1319 questions (`tests/evals/gsm8k/gsm8k_eval.py`): Qwen3-30B-A3B-GPTQ-Int4 85.90% → 86.13%; OLMoE-1B-7B (base model, near the floor with this script) 9.93% → 10.01%. Invalid rate 0–0.8%.
- CI: the L4 (sm89) "MoE Kernels" step runs `tests/kernels/moe` on `csrc/moe/` changes and covers the launch without the attribute; the SM90+ launch is unchanged. No new test: there is no functional change, and a regression check would need graph-edge inspection or timing, which does not belong in `tests/`.

**Op chain, CUDA graph, µs per replay** (median of 6 rounds, A/B/B/A order; Δ = median paired `fix − rebuilt`)

| shape (experts, top-k, hidden, layers) | tokens | base | rebuilt | fix | Δ |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| Qwen3.8-Flash-Next (512, 10, 2560, 48) | 1 / 16 / 48 | 843 / 893 / 917 | 846 / 894 / 916 | 782 / 831 / 850 | −7.6% / −6.9% / −7.2% |
| Qwen3-30B-A3B (128, 8, 2048, 48) | 1 / 16 / 48 | 592 / 672 / 688 | 596 / 674 / 691 | 542 / 620 / 636 | −9.0% / −7.9% / −8.0% |
| OLMoE-1B-7B (64, 8, 2048, 16) | 1 / 16 / 48 | 194 / 209 / 221 | 194 / 209 / 221 | 177 / 192 / 204 | −8.7% / −8.4% / −7.8% |

**End to end, `vllm bench latency`** (input 128, output 256, 3 rounds, ms per step)

| model | batch | base | rebuilt | fix | Δ |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---|
| OLMoE-1B-7B-0924 | 1 | 2.952 | 2.950 | 2.932 | −0.7% (3/3 rounds vs rebuilt, 2/3 vs base) |
| OLMoE-1B-7B-0924 | 16 | 7.789 | 7.731 | 7.802 | within noise |
| Qwen3-30B-A3B-GPTQ-Int4 | 1 | 5.805 | – | 5.722 | −1.2% (3/3 rounds) |
| Qwen3-30B-A3B-GPTQ-Int4 | 16 | 12.188 | – | 12.136 | within noise (2/3 rounds faster) |

<details>
<summary>TP4 setup</summary>

v0.33.0, 4× A100-PCIE-40GB, `--tensor-parallel-size 4 --enable-expert-parallel`, NVFP4 weights, MTP with 2 draft tokens, `--compilation-config '{"mode": 0, "cudagraph_mode": "FULL_DECODE_ONLY"}'`, bf16 KV, a custom logits processor. Client: c concurrent streaming chat requests, 384 output tokens, model-default sampling; per-request decode = (tokens − 1) / (last − first token time), averaged. Prose / code / numbers prompts × c = 1, 2, 4, 8, 12, 16; two server starts per arm, A/B/B/A. With MTP, c = 1 varies by about ±10% from run to run through the draft acceptance rate.

</details>

<details>
<summary>Standalone CUDA reproduction (no vLLM) and commands</summary>

48 × (plain kernel → consumer kernel); only the consumer launch changes. A100, 21 rounds:

| consumer launch | graph replay, GPU µs | eager, GPU µs |
|---|---:|---:|
| `<<<>>>` | 128.7 | 239.8 |
| `cudaLaunchKernelEx`, no attribute | 128.7 | 239.3 |
| `cudaLaunchKernelEx` + PDL attribute | 181.8 | 239.8 |
| PDL attribute on the first consumer only | 130.3 | 239.4 |

Same harness, graph replay, other pre-Hopper GPUs (21 rounds, PDL attribute slower in every round):

| GPU (arch) | `<<<>>>` µs | + PDL attribute | per edge | `cudaLaunchKernelEx`, no attribute |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| A100-PCIE-40GB (sm80) | 128.7 | +53.1 (+41%) | 1.1 µs | +0.03 |
| RTX A4000 (sm86) | 83.6 | +29.9 (+36%) | 0.62 µs | +0.11 |
| RTX 4090 (sm89) | 79.0 | +30.0 (+38%) | 0.63 µs | −0.10 |

`cudaGraphGetEdges` reports one programmatic edge per PDL launch on all three. The standalone harness and the op-chain script are in https://gist.github.com/srkim-business/ec5db57f7b78a9c9f06af65c891216c2.

```bash
# end to end (OLMoE-1B-7B-0924 and Qwen3-30B-A3B-GPTQ-Int4, batch 1 and 16)
vllm bench latency --model <model> --batch-size <1|16> --input-len 128 --output-len 256 \
  --num-iters-warmup 5 --num-iters 15 --seed 0 --max-model-len 1024 --gpu-memory-utilization 0.85
# GSM8K
vllm serve <model> --max-model-len 4096 --gpu-memory-utilization 0.85 --seed 0
python tests/evals/gsm8k/gsm8k_eval.py --port 8000 --seed 42 --num-questions 1319 --max-concurrency 64
# kernel tests
pytest tests/kernels/moe/test_fused_topk.py
```

</details>

## Details

- Root cause: on pre-SM90 the attribute does nothing for eager launches, but stream capture records it as a programmatic edge (`cudaGraphGetEdges` counts one per launch on sm80). Each edge adds about 1.1 µs of GPU time per graph replay on A100.
- #59737 first had this host check (uncached); review asked to drop it for consistency with `topk_softplus_sqrt` / `per_token_group_quant` and to avoid `cudaGetDevice` + `call_once` per eager launch. The measurements above are the reason to bring it back. It is cached in a function-local static as in `fused_deepseek_v4_qnorm_rope_kv_insert_kernel.cu` (`numAttrs = (sm_version >= 90) ? 1 : 0`), so eager launches pay nothing per call. This also matches the scope in #59737's own description ("Enable PDL for the consumer on SM90+"). Python launch sites already gate PDL on `current_platform.is_arch_support_pdl()`.
- The static is initialized once per template instantiation, on the device the caller's `DeviceGuard` selects. It assumes all GPUs in a process share the major arch, which holds for vLLM workers (one GPU each); a mismatch would only affect speed, not results.
- The 1-GPU gain (about 1%) matches the GPU-side edge cost. The TP4 + EP + MTP gain does not: at concurrency 16 a decode step goes from about 29.5 to 27.3 ms, while 48 edges × 1.1 µs is about 0.05 ms per forward; we have not located the rest. The TP4 A/B swaps only `_moe_C` (shipped → this diff built from the same source); on one GPU a no-change rebuild is within 0.8% (median) of the shipped build, so we attribute the gain to this diff.
- Other C++ launchers still set the attribute on all archs, for example `topk_softplus_sqrt_kernels.cu` and `per_token_group_quant.cu` (the latter can run on sm89 for FP8). They are left out to keep this fix small enough to cherry-pick; a shared helper can follow if maintainers prefer.
- Not a duplicate: no open issue or PR changes this launch attribute (searched `topkGating PDL`, `topk_softmax PDL`, `59737`). #62912 (open) changes top-k selection in the same file and keeps `config.numAttrs = 1` as context next to this change, so whichever lands second needs a small rebase; it does not touch the attribute.
- Not covered: Hopper/Blackwell (unchanged code path, not measured), sm75 and older, end to end on GPUs other than A100, and a full main build (only `_moe_C` was rebuilt and overlaid on v0.33.0).
- This is a performance regression against v0.32.0; we'd like it cherry-picked into a v0.33.x patch release if one is planned.
- I used AI assistance (Claude) for the investigation, the code and the tests. I reviewed every changed line and ran the tests and GPU checks above.

## Overview

Lists NVIDIA Parakeet TDT (`ParakeetForTDT`, e.g. `nvidia/parakeet-tdt-0.6b-v3`) as supported through the out-of-tree [vllm-parakeet-plugin](https://github.com/Alex-Wengg/vllm-parakeet-plugin), the same route as Nemotron 3.5 ASR in #59827. Refs #23943.

## Claims

- `ParakeetForTDT` is listed in the plugin table in `supported_models.md` and with the other plugin-backed encoder-decoder models in `v1_guide.md`.
- No vLLM code changes.

## Validation

The plugin on vLLM 0.32.0, one RTX A6000:

| Check | Result |
| --- | --- |
| Token parity vs Transformers `generate()`, 73 LibriSpeech clips, fp32 (`scripts/parity.py`) | 73/73 identical |
| WER through `vllm serve` (bf16 encoder), LibriSpeech test-clean / test-other (`scripts/eval_wer.py`) | 1.93% / 3.61% (model card: 1.93% / 3.59%) |
| Throughput through `vllm serve`, 64 concurrent requests, test-clean | RTFx 238 |

`pre-commit run --files docs/models/supported_models.md docs/usage/v1_guide.md` passes.

## Details

- Not a duplicate of #41708 (with MRV2 `ModelState` work), the first Parakeet TDT integration, which has been waiting since September on a decision about native support. That PR decodes each transcript at prefill and replays it as forced tokens. The plugin instead decodes step by step, batched across requests, and adds no model code to vLLM.
- The plugin follows the layout of [vllm-nemotron-asr-plugin](https://github.com/Sohaib-Ahmed21/vllm-nemotron-asr-plugin): a `vllm.general_plugins` entry point, a `VerifyAndUpdateConfig` hook, an MRV2 `ModelState` that keeps each request's encoder frames, the decode loop inside `forward`, and one-hot `compute_logits`. It differs in two ways. The TDT loop advances all requests together in GPU tensors and applies TDT's frame-skip durations. The plugin also captures its own CUDA graphs, so it runs with plain `vllm serve` and needs no `--enforce-eager` or `VLLM_USE_V2_MODEL_RUNNER=1`.
- Unlike #59827, this adds no `_OOT_SUPPORTED_MODELS` entry. Transformers defines `ParakeetForTDT`, so without the plugin, vLLM resolves the model to the Transformers backend before it checks that table, and the entry would never be used.

commits.pr_title: [ROCm][CI] Fix Muse Spark RoPE cache leak between tests
commits.pr_body:
## Overview

Fixes the remaining 26 `tests/models/test_muse_spark_rocm_mono.py` failures in `:amd: (MI355) Basic Models (Other)` on the [nightly build #99098](https://buildkite.com/vllm/ci/builds/99098/list?sid=01a19b12-86dc-48ba-811c-30a4d4e009ed). `test_muse_spark_rocm_shared_rope.py` leaves a CPU `RotaryEmbedding` in `get_rope`'s global cache, and the mono test's tiny GPU model picks it up when both files run in the same pytest session, as they do in that shard. The other 2 failures in the job (`test_layer_guards_follow_the_weight_finalize`, `test_weight_views_alias_the_rank_slices`) are fixed by #65080.

## Claims

- `test_muse_spark_rocm_shared_rope.py` runs with its own empty `_ROPE_DICT`, so its CPU RoPE no longer leaks into later tests.
- Together with #65080, `test_muse_spark_rocm_mono.py` passes when it runs after the shared-RoPE test.
- Test-only change: no model or kernel code is touched.

## Validation

MI355X (gfx950), using the ROCm wheel from build #99098 (`0e5b2ba11`) with `vllm/models/muse_spark/amd/model.py` from current `main` (#65080):

```bash
pytest -v tests/models/test_muse_spark_rocm_shared_rope.py tests/models/test_muse_spark_rocm_mono.py
```

| Run | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| `test_muse_spark_rocm_mono.py` alone | 33 passed | 33 passed |
| `shared_rope` then `mono` | 26 failed, 8 passed | 34 passed |

Before, all 26 failures are `RuntimeError: fused_muse_spark_qknorm_rope_kv_insert, ...: cos_sin_cache must be a contiguous 2-D CUDA tensor`, the same as in CI. The four Muse Spark files in CI order (`rocm_loading`, `logits_local`, `shared_rope`, `mono`) give 48 passed. `ruff check` and `ruff format --check` pass.

## Details

- `get_rope()` caches `RotaryEmbedding` objects in the global `_ROPE_DICT` without the device in the key, so the CPU RoPE created by `test_muse_spark_rocm_shared_rope.py` stays in the cache after that test. The tiny GPU model in `test_muse_spark_rocm_mono.py` then gets that CPU RoPE, and `fused_muse_spark_qknorm_rope_kv_insert` fails because `cos_sin_cache` is not on the GPU.

commits.pr_title: [Rust Frontend] Accept duplicate reasoning aliases in chat messages
commits.pr_body:
## Overview

Fixes #63130: the Rust frontend rejected chat requests whose assistant message carries **both** `reasoning` and `reasoning_content` with an opaque serde `duplicate field` parse error, while the Python frontend accepts the identical body. This permanently breaks multi-turn agent loops because the offending assistant turn stays in history and every follow-up request fails.

The fix normalizes the reasoning aliases to the primary `reasoning` field in `ChatMessage::deserialize` before dispatching to the derived impl, mirroring the Python frontend's `_normalize_messages_before` (`vllm/entrypoints/openai/chat_completion/protocol.py:556`).

## Claims

- A chat request with an assistant message carrying `reasoning` + `reasoning_content` (in any key order, plus the `thinking` alias) is now accepted, matching the Python frontend's behavior matrix from the issue.
- Non-null `reasoning` wins (including an empty string); a JSON-null `reasoning` falls back to `reasoning_content`, exactly mirroring the Python normalization semantics.
- The thinking text is carried exactly once into the rendered assistant reasoning block.

## Validation

Reproducer from the issue (both keys together) and the alias precedence matrix (key order, null and empty `reasoning`, wrong-type alias, `thinking`) are covered by one table-driven test at the deserialization layer, `assistant_reasoning_aliases_fold_into_reasoning`:

```bash
cargo test -p vllm-server --lib
# test result: ok. 504 passed; 0 failed
```

Regression proof: with the `normalize_reasoning_aliases` call removed, `assistant_reasoning_aliases_fold_into_reasoning` fails because alias values no longer reach `reasoning`; restored, all tests pass. `cargo fmt --check` and `cargo clippy -p vllm-server --all-targets -- -D warnings` are clean.

## Details

**Root cause.** `ChatMessage::Assistant` declares `reasoning` with `#[serde(alias = "reasoning_content")]` / `#[serde(alias = "thinking")]`. Serde's derived `Deserialize` treats every key mapping to one field as a candidate and raises `duplicate field` when two of them appear, before any normalization can run. The Python frontend instead pops `reasoning_content` in a `model_validator(mode="before")` and fills `reasoning` only when it is absent/null, so the same payload is accepted there.

**Fix.** The manual `Deserialize` impl already materializes each message as a `serde_json::Value` for role dispatch; a small `normalize_reasoning_aliases` step runs on that value first (removes both alias keys, promotes the first non-null alias when `reasoning` is absent/null). Because it is key-based rather than order-based, it is deterministic regardless of client key order. The `#[serde(alias)]` attributes are removed, so this step is the only place that defines the alias set.

**Intentional deviation (Python parity note).** The Python frontend does not normalize a top-level `thinking` string on messages (it is an unknown field there), while the Rust frontend deliberately accepts it as an alias. The collision handling therefore orders precedence as `reasoning` > `reasoning_content` > `thinking`, keeping the existing Rust-only `thinking` extension but making it tolerant of duplicates too.

**Not duplicating an existing PR.** Verified with `gh pr list --search "63130 in:body"` (0 results) and issue search; no open PR addresses this. Note: a comment on the issue mentions a similar effort in progress; this PR is a narrow, tested fix at the same layer and is offered in case it is useful — happy to yield or rebase on a competing approach if maintainers prefer.

**Limitation.** This restores wire-level acceptance parity for the reasoning alias family. The Python frontend's separate semantic rejection of typed `thinking` content blocks combined with top-level `reasoning` (PR #41718) is not ported here; that is a distinct validation concern and would merit its own change.

commits.pr_title: [Bugfix][Rust Frontend][ZMQ] Run ZMQ transport I/O on the dedicated runtime
commits.pr_body:
## Overview

Create and connect Rust frontend ZMQ sockets on the dedicated runtime so
socket readiness and background transport tasks use the same Tokio I/O
driver. Caller-runtime load or shutdown can no longer delay or terminate
engine communication.



## Claims

- Registers HandshakeOwner and Bootstrapped transport I/O with the dedicated
  ZMQ runtime instead of the runtime that calls `EngineCoreClient::connect`.
- Keeps engine communication functional after the connecting runtime is shut
  down.
- Preserves the existing transport protocol, configuration, and public API.
- Retains cancellation safety while connection setup runs on the dedicated
  runtime.



## Validation

```
cargo nextest run --locked -p vllm-engine-core-client \
  client_transport_outlives_connecting_runtime
```


A Linux epoll probe with a mock engine confirmed the runtime ownership change:

| Measurement | Before | After |
|---|---:|---:|
| ZMQ TCP descriptors on the connecting runtime | 4 | 0 |
| ZMQ TCP descriptors on the dedicated runtime | 0 | 4 |
| Output delay while the connecting runtime was blocked | ~4.70 s | 0.43–0.75 ms |




## Details

Tokio associates TCP resources with the I/O driver of the runtime active when
those resources are created. Transport setup previously ran on the caller
runtime, while `build_zmq_runtime()` was called only after the sockets had
already been bound or connected. Background transport tasks ran on the
dedicated runtime, but socket readiness was still driven by the caller
runtime.

The dedicated runtime is now created before transport setup. The complete
connection path runs on that runtime, and the same runtime is passed into
`from_connected` for background task execution and lifetime ownership.

commits.pr_title: [Bugfix][KV Offload] Anchor the partial-tail lookup on the full-attention prefix
commits.pr_body:
## Purpose

Split out of #57216 per @orozery's review (part 1 of 2): the lookup half. The DCP store half is #58619.

`_lookup` anchors the partial-tail search on `_lookup_complete_chunks`, which requires *every* KV cache group to have a complete chunk at the anchor boundary, including the recurrent groups. A recurrent `align` group holds state only where a scheduler step ended on one of its block boundaries: in practice at the producer prompt's last full recurrent block and at its tail.

With **uniform block sizes** (dcp=1, the only shape `supports_partial_tail` admits today) the last-full-block boundary is also a full-attention chunk multiple, so that aligned row lands on the chunk grid, `complete_hit` reaches it, and the existing one-window probe finds the tail. The anchor only fails when that row is missing, e.g. evicted separately from the tail. So on `main` today this is a robustness fix.

With **mixed block sizes** -- under DCP the full-attention offload block is `dcp x` the attention block while recurrent blocks stay unsharded (12288 vs 1536 at DCP 8) -- the aligned row sits at a recurrent multiple that is essentially never a full-attention multiple. `complete_hit` is then 0 for any prompt past the first chunk, the search is capped at one window from zero, and a correctly stored tail further out is never probed although it is resident. That is the state #58619 (the DCP store side) would land in without this PR: tails get stored, but only those within one window of the complete-chunk hit are ever found -- the "#58619 only" column of the hardware table below. **This PR is the prerequisite for #58619's lookups to work.**

Instrumented `_lookup` on a replay (chunk 12288, hash 128), before the change:

```
n=12620  complete_hit=12288  complete_boundary=12288  max_boundary=12544
           boundary=12544 ALL GROUPS HIT                  <- restores
n=15136  complete_hit=0      complete_boundary=0      max_boundary=12160
           boundary=12160 group=0 MISS ... 11776 MISS     <- tail stored at 15104,
                                                            never probed
```

Fix: anchor the partial-tail search on the boundary the full-attention groups proved, which `_lookup_complete_chunks` already returns (since #63566), and check recurrent groups only at the candidate boundary. Per review, the search runs from one window past the anchor down to the complete-chunk hit and skips block-aligned boundaries (complete chunks, which the complete-chunk lookup already missed), so a longer full-attention prefix stored by another request cannot hide this request's own tail. If a full-attention chunk between the complete hit and the anchor is still being loaded, the search falls back to the complete hit. No second lookup and no new parameters.

The reported hit is never shorter than the complete-chunk hit, so the change can only widen what a lookup reports. Pending full-attention chunks are handled exactly as in the complete-chunk lookup on `main`.

## Test Plan

Unit tests on the existing dcp=1 hybrid fixture (`_make_partial_tail_scheduler`: 16-token full-attention and Mamba blocks, hash 4):

```
pytest tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/offloading_connector/ -q
```

- tail found with no recurrent state at the chunk boundary (30-token prompt, tail at 28)
- the same across **two** complete chunks (46-token prompt, tail at 44): the production shape, where the complete-chunk anchor is 0
- a longer full-attention prefix stored by another request does not hide this request's own tail, including when that prefix covers the whole prompt (per review)
- the load path requests only the verified chunk keys plus the tail keys
- `max_num_new_tokens` caps which tail the search may report
- a tail is found after a GPU prefix hit
- 0 when no tail was stored; 0 when the full-attention chunk is not resident
- the tail is preferred over an aligned recurrent state at the chunk boundary
- the search falls back while the anchor chunk is being loaded

## Test Result

**Unit tests** (`pytest tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/offloading_connector/`, GB300, same image), base `main` @ e318ac0979:

| tree | result |
|---|---|
| `main` | 690 passed, 3 failed |
| this PR | 707 passed, 3 failed |
| this PR + #58619 | 721 passed, 3 failed |

The 3 failures are the same on `main` at this commit: `test_partial_tail_store_uses_attention_and_recurrent_cow_sources` and `test_eagle_partial_tail_round_trip_serves_mamba_checkpoint[True/False]` expect a recurrent group's CPU `BlockStored.block_size` of 0, which is 4 since #62613. `pre-commit` (ruff, mypy) passes.

**Hardware** (1 x GB300 node, `vllm/vllm-openai:nightly-2b009fc6`; "fix" overlays the branch's `vllm/`, "main" is the stock nightly). Model: Kimi-Linear-48B-A3B-Instruct (KDA + MLA), TP2, `--mamba-cache-mode align --prefix-match-unit 128`, OffloadingConnector with a 16 GiB CPU pool. "fix" is this PR + #58619.

Protocol per prompt: clear all tiers, cold run (asserted 0 cached), reset only the GPU prefix cache, replay. The table shows tokens restored from the CPU tier, i.e. the replay delta of `vllm:prompt_tokens_by_source{source="external_kv_transfer"}`.

| 12549 | 12544 | 12544 | 12288 | **12544** |

An earlier run of the combined change on a 2-node GB300 K3 deployment (TP8/DCP8) is in #57216.

## Notes

commits.pr_title: [Bugfix][Rust Frontend] Match Python text-part joining for HF templates
commits.pr_body:
## Overview

The Rust HF renderer currently turns `["Part one. ", "Part two."]` into `"Part one. Part two."`, while Python inserts a newline. When an HF template expects string content, this change renders each content part as one segment (a media part as its placeholder, in place), skips empty text parts, and joins the segments with `\n`.

Addresses the HF `ChatContent::Parts` case in item 1 of #63917.

## Claims

- Text-only content lists use Python's newline separator, skip empty parts, and preserve whitespace within each part.
- Lists with media keep each placeholder at its part's position and use the same separator, which matches Python's output with `--interleave-mm-strings` (pinned by `tests/renderers/chat_utils/test_image.py::test_parse_chat_messages_multiple_images_interleave`). Python's default moves placeholders to the front; Rust intentionally keeps them where the client put them.
- Renderer tests pin the joined string for text-only lists, image, video and audio placeholders, and the Step-5 VL template in string format. Existing tests cover automatic and explicit string formats and OpenAI-format content, which still passes the parts list to the template.

## Validation

On Linux aarch64, Rust 1.95:

```sh
cargo nextest run --manifest-path rust/Cargo.toml --workspace
# 2436 passed, 13 skipped

cargo clippy --manifest-path rust/Cargo.toml -p vllm-chat -p vllm-server --all-targets -- -D warnings
# passed

cargo fmt --manifest-path rust/Cargo.toml --all --check
# passed
```

Changing the final `join("\n")` back to plain concatenation fails six renderer tests:

```text
renderer::hf::tests::chat_template_flattens_text_parts_for_string_templates
renderer::hf::tests::chat_template_forces_string_content_format_when_configured
renderer::hf::tests::string_content_format_replaces_image_with_placeholder_text
renderer::hf::tests::string_content_format_replaces_video_with_placeholder_text
renderer::hf::tests::string_content_format_replaces_audio_with_placeholder_text
renderer::hf::tests::step5_vl_template_places_im_patch_at_image_part_position_string_format
```

I also ran Python's `parse_chat_messages` with a local Qwen3 config and the checked-in Qwen3 template: five cases passed, covering multiple parts, empty parts, existing newlines, a single part, and empty text. The issue's input rendered as:

```text
'<|im_start|>user\nPart one. \nPart two.<|im_end|>\n<|im_start|>assistant\n'
```

Validation reaches prompt rendering; real-model generation/quality evaluation was not run. The existing Rust Cargo CI job runs the affected test suites.

## Details

The separator belongs in the HF string renderer. The shared content-flattening helper is also used by model-specific renderers, so changing it would widen the behavior change. One rule now covers text-only and mixed lists, so adding media to a list does not change how its text parts are joined. This patch leaves assistant output-block aggregation and other renderers outside its scope; it does not close the whole issue.

The first revision's route test and docs paragraph were dropped: the renderer unit tests pin the joined string where it is produced, and the Rust frontend now follows Python's existing behavior, which needs no user-facing note.

Duplicate-work check: #63762 changes DeepSeek V4/V4.1 rendering; #63926 addresses items 2 and 3. Neither covers this HF path. Scope was also noted in the issue.

commits.pr_title: [Rust Frontend] Run utility calls to completion when the caller is cancelled
commits.pr_body:
## Purpose

`EngineCoreClient::call_utility` fans a utility request out to every engine and waits for the replies. Dropping its future ran `UtilityCallGuard`, which unregistered the waiters, but since vllm-project/vllm#46051 each request is sent by a task on the client's ZMQ runtime, so requests already handed off were still sent and the engines executed them. Cancellation only abandoned the client-side bookkeeping, and the replies arrived with no waiter.

So a caller cannot tie state to a call's completion: anything it holds is released when its future is dropped, which can be before the engines see the request. vllm-project/vllm#63870 needs exactly that: readiness withdrawn for a pause must stay withdrawn until the engines have handled it, even if the HTTP or gRPC client that sent `/pause` disconnects.

This PR makes a utility call run to completion once its requests are prepared. The first commit moves the fan-out unchanged from `EngineCoreClient` to `ClientInner`, which owns the socket; the second changes it:

- The caller registers the waiters and encodes the requests, borrowing the arguments.
- One task on the client runtime sends the requests directly and collects every reply, so a utility call spawns once rather than once per engine through `send_to_engine`. The task unregisters the waiters of requests that failed to send.
- The caller awaits that task and decodes the replies, so neither the arguments nor the result type need `'static`.

Dropping the returned future now only stops waiting. `UtilityCallGuard` is removed. A call that fails while preparing still unregisters the waiters it allocated. If the client runtime shuts down during a call, the caller gets a `ClientClosed` error.

Not a duplicate: no open PR changes Rust utility call cancellation (searched `rust utility call cancel` and `call_utility`).

## Test Plan

- `cancelled_utility_call_unregisters_waiter` becomes `cancelled_utility_call_still_collects_the_reply`: after the caller is aborted, the waiter stays until the engine replies, and the reply then resolves it. It fails on `main`, where the abort unregisters the waiter.
- `cargo nextest run --workspace` in `rust/`, plus `cargo clippy --workspace --tests --examples -- -D warnings` and `cargo fmt --check`.

## Test Result

- `cargo nextest run --workspace`: 2376 passed, 13 skipped.
- clippy and fmt passed.

No model evaluation: generated tokens are unaffected.

## Overview

Add a new Triton kernel for fused norm+quant MXFP8. To simplify integration, this kernel also covers additional no-quantize callsites:
- norm+quant before QKV proj
- No quantize: Input norm, final norm, MTP enorm/hnorm

dspark drafter's per-head norms remain on FlashInfer kernels.

## Claims

- MXFP8 norm + quantization: 1.39–1.60× faster than the norm → quantize chain across M=1–16K tokens (launch-bound at small M); 6.46 TB/s at M=16K tokens (~96% of the 6.76 TB/s streaming ceiling).
- BF16 norm: faster than FlashInfer at all but one measured M (plain M=1024 tokens: 0.99×, noise level).
- Bitwise residuals/UE8M0 scales; E4M3 code distance ≤1; BF16-out within 1 BF16 ulp.
- GSM8K accuracy: 0.9360 vs 0.9380 base (1-question delta, within noise). E2E prefill TTFT p50 is 0.4–0.9% lower at c=1/16 and neutral at c=4; decode TPOT p50 is neutral at c=32 and 5.4–9.6% lower at c=128/512 (2 rounds per arm).

## Validation

- `.venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/models/minimax_m3/test_norm_mxfp8.py -v` → **13 passed** on GB300.
- `pre-commit`: all hooks passed.

### Microbenchmark

### E2E serving

- `vllm bench serve`; MiniMax-M3.1-Flash on GB300; base = `upstream/main`, PR = this branch.
- 2 full runs per arm; ranges shown.
- Decode used the mega MoE backend (`--moe-backend deep_gemm_mega_moe`); both configs use dspark speculative decoding.

**Prefill:** PP2 TP1, 100k-token random prefix + 8k-token input, 1 output token.

| ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| 1 | 288.0 ms | 286.5–286.9 ms | 0.4–0.5% |

| Concurrency | Base TPOT p50 | PR TPOT p50 | Speedup |

| Config | Accuracy |
| --- | ---: |
| upstream/main | 0.9380 |
| This PR | 0.9360 |

## Details

- `MiniMAXGemmaRMSNorm.forward` calls the Triton kernel (`ops/norm_mxfp8.py`) via `gemma_rmsnorm_mxfp8(x, weight, eps, residual=None, mxfp8=True)`.
- Non-2-D inputs (the dspark drafter per-head norms, e.g. (16384, 4, 128)) keep the FlashInfer kernels.
- `forward_input_norm` passes `mxfp8=True` when `get_input_quant_key(qkv_proj) == kMxfp8Dynamic` with a supported FlashInfer MXFP8 linear kernel.
- TP>1 keeps the fused all-reduce + norm path; that helper's TP1 branch calls the norm module, so it uses Triton too.
- Kernel: hidden size is `tl.constexpr`; token count is `do_not_specialize` (2 compiled variants total: MXFP8 on/off). Specializes on `None` residual/`sf` pointers instead of constexpr flags; asserts 2-D row-contiguous inputs, with arbitrary row stride supported.
- PDL: every CTA calls `gdc_wait` before any global access, then `gdc_launch_dependents`.
- Model-local to MiniMax-M3 NVIDIA; no new flags or dependencies.
