## Overview

With `--monokernel`, Muse Spark Open MXFP4 on 8x MI355X (TP8 + expert parallelism, 7-token DSpark draft) runs
decoder layers 1-60 of every verify step of 1-16 requests as persistent FlyDSL launches. One launch, or three, cover
the work from a layer's attention output to the next layer's q, o-gate and KV insert. All other steps and layers 0 and
61 run the stock path. The flag is off by default.

## Claims

- AgentX (agentic-coding traces, DSpark at synthetic acceptance length 4.05, all requests, full mode), this PR's head
  with `--monokernel` vs the faster stock recipe on its base (main 3d81a51): interactivity (1000 / p90 ITL) / total
  tok/s/GPU of 413.8 / 2974 vs 263.1 / 2325 at c = 1 (+57 % / +28 %), 314.1 / 3056 vs 232.7 / 2368 at c = 2
  (+35 % / +29 %), 295.2 / 4430 vs 217.3 / 3585 at c = 4 (+36 % / +24 %) and 208.4 / 7384 vs 143.3 / 6126 at c = 8
  (+45 % / +21 %).
- Accuracy contract (GPQA-Diamond, AIME25, RULER NIAH; method of #60397), `--monokernel` vs stock: GPQA-Diamond
  88.7 vs 88.5 (delta +0.1 ± 0.5; boxed-letter prompt -0.7 ± 0.6), AIME25 98.6 vs 98.3 (+0.3 ± 0.4), RULER NIAH 348 vs 346 of 360.
- Accuracy and DSpark acceptance, real acceptance, stock (main 3d81a51) and `--monokernel` (c0f424a) with the same
  server flags: GSM8K (full set, 5-shot) 0.9651-0.9735 with `--monokernel` and 0.9666-0.9742 stock at c = 1-16, mean
  acceptance length 4.512 vs 4.431. Long-context needle retrieval at 33k-529k tokens: 192/192 in both arms, mean
  acceptance length 3.638 vs 3.600.
- Opt-in only. If the deployment is not supported, vLLM refuses it at startup with every reason. Steps that the
  kernels do not cover run stock. Nothing changes without `--monokernel`.

## Validation

All runs: c0f424a (`--monokernel`) and its base, main 3d81a51 (stock), on the vLLM ROCm nightly image 00b6c4c (AITER
0.1.26) with the Python files of each commit, 8x MI355X. After these runs, the head e2ed1f0 removes redundant code and
adds two startup refusals (sleep mode, weight transfer): all 30 builds compile to identical `.text`, and the 26
monokernel code objects that its server loads have the same sha1 as on c0f424a. On 49485cc (the head without the two
refusals): GSM8K c = 8 0.9674 with acceptance length 4.495; AgentX fast mode vs c0f424a 328.8 / 2867 vs 330.5 / 2865
at c = 1 and 209.2 / 6135 vs 215.4 / 6151 at c = 8 (fast-mode noise).

### Performance: AgentX

Server: the recipe's Muse Spark Open MXFP4 command on 8x MI355X with the DSpark draft. Changes for the benchmark:
`--max-model-len 1048576 --max-num-seqs 16`, `--enable-prefix-caching`, and synthetic acceptance
(`"rejection_sample_method":"synthetic","synthetic_acceptance_length":4.05`). The `--monokernel` server is TEP8.
Stock runs the recipe's two strategies: plain TP8 (with `--max-num-seqs 8`, the recipe's 1M-context TP setting; the
recipe's lowest-latency choice for one request) and TEP8 (the same command as the `--monokernel` arm without
`--monokernel`). Benchmark: `agentx profile --public-dataset semianalysis_cc_traces_weka_062126 --concurrency C`. This
dataset is agentic-coding traces with an ISL p50 of 159k tokens and a maximum of 397k. Metrics are over all
requests: interactivity = 1000 / p90 ITL (tok/s/user) and total tok/s/GPU.

Full mode (`--benchmark-duration 3600 --warmup-requests-per-lane 10`), one run a point. Each cell: interactivity /
total tok/s/GPU (p90 ITL in ms, requests):

| c | `--monokernel` (TEP8) | stock TP8 | stock TEP8 | `--monokernel` vs the faster stock |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | 413.8 / 2974 (2.42, 291) | 263.1 / 2325 (3.80, 256) | | +57 % / +28 % |
| 2 | 314.1 / 3056 (3.18, 474) | 232.7 / 2368 (4.30, 398) | 223.5 / 2367 (4.47, 398) | +35 % / +29 % |
| 4 | 295.2 / 4430 (3.39, 668) | 217.3 / 3585 (4.60, 580) | 212.5 / 3392 (4.71, 557) | +36 % / +24 % |
| 8 | 208.4 / 7384 (4.80, 1362) | | 143.3 / 6126 (6.98, 1176) | +45 % / +21 % |

Stock TP8 at c = 8 and stock TEP8 at c = 1 were not run (the recipe names TEP8 the faster choice from a few
concurrent requests, and TP8 for one request). This PR does not measure c >= 16.

### Accuracy

Real acceptance (the recipe's block verification), stock and `--monokernel` with the same server flags: TEP8
(`--tensor-parallel-size 8 --enable-expert-parallel`) in both arms; the only difference is `--monokernel`. The
acceptance length is the DSpark mean acceptance length from the server's `/metrics` over each run.

GSM8K = InferenceX gsm8k.yaml, full set (1319), 5-shot, prefix caching off (flexible-extract; strict-match differs by
0.0008 at most). Output tok/s = the generated tokens (from `/metrics`) / the wall time of the run:

| c | GSM8K stock | GSM8K mono | acceptance length stock | acceptance length mono | output tok/s stock | output tok/s mono |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | 0.9666 | 0.9666 | 4.533 | 4.570 | 300 | 480 |
| 2 | 0.9719 | 0.9735 | 4.488 | 4.465 | 520 | 662 |
| 4 | 0.9719 | 0.9697 | 4.461 | 4.524 | 862 | 1124 |
| 8 | 0.9712 | 0.9704 | 4.400 | 4.422 | 1329 | 1465 |
| 16 | 0.9742 | 0.9651 | 4.273 | 4.577 | 1973 | 2125 |
| mean | 0.9712 | 0.9691 | 4.431 | 4.512 | | |

The stderr of one GSM8K score is about 0.005; the per-c differences go both ways. Three more runs at c = 16 (on the
head e2ed1f0): stock 0.9682 / 0.9689 / 0.9704, `--monokernel` 0.9727 / 0.9727 / 0.9742.

With the AgentX server flags (prefix caching on), GSM8K at c = 8: stock 0.9682 with acceptance length 4.526,
`--monokernel` 0.9704 with 4.426.

Long context: multi-key needle retrieval. Each prompt hides 8 seven-digit numbers in filler text and asks for one;
the answer is scored by exact match. 12 prompts at each length, each run at c = 1, 2, 4 and 8, prefix caching on:

| context | correct stock | correct mono | acceptance length stock | acceptance length mono |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 33k | 48/48 | 48/48 | 3.525 | 3.648 |
| 132k | 48/48 | 48/48 | 3.649 | 3.607 |
| 264k | 48/48 | 48/48 | 3.620 | 3.672 |
| 529k | 48/48 | 48/48 | 3.623 | 3.627 |

The answers are short (about 360 tokens), so the acceptance length is lower than on GSM8K in both arms.

#### Accuracy contract: GPQA-Diamond, AIME25, RULER NIAH

Method of #60397 / RFC #59665: pass@1, the same build and server flags in both arms (TEP8, DSpark with real
acceptance, prefix caching on, 8 requests in flight); stock = main 3d81a51, `--monokernel` = the head
e2ed1f0. ± is the standard error across questions; delta is mono - stock, paired by question.

| | stock | `--monokernel` | delta |
|---|---|---|---|
| GPQA-Diamond, the GPQA authors' prompt (16 samples a question) | 88.5 ± 1.8 | 88.7 ± 1.8 | +0.1 ± 0.5 |
| GPQA-Diamond, boxed-letter prompt (16 samples a question) | 86.4 ± 1.8 | 85.7 ± 1.8 | -0.7 ± 0.6 |
| AIME25 (32 samples a problem) | 98.3 ± 0.7 | 98.6 ± 0.7 | +0.3 ± 0.4 |
| RULER NIAH (single, multikey 2 and 3 at 32K / 128K / 256K, 40 a cell) | 346/360 | 348/360 | |

- GPQA-Diamond: InferenceX's questions (each in 2 option orders), 8 seeds, `reasoning_effort` xhigh, temperature
  1.0, top-k 64 (the model's generation config), 64K tokens. First row: the zero-shot prompt and answer parser of the
  GPQA authors' repository. Second row: a "put the letter in `\boxed{}`" instruction, graded with InferenceX's
  last-letter rule. With 4 seeds per arm the delta moved from -1.3 (seeds 0-3) to +1.5 (seeds 4-7) on the same prompt,
  so the seed-to-seed spread is larger than the per-question standard error.
- AIME25: lm-eval's `aime25` with the boxed-answer instruction, `reasoning_effort` high, temperature 0.6, top-p 0.95,
  64K tokens, 32 seeds.
- RULER NIAH: lm-eval's RULER tasks, greedy, `reasoning_effort` high, 32K tokens, every needle must be in the answer.
  The misses are the same kinds in both arms (stock 11 / mono 8 with an empty answer, 3 / 4 with a distractor key).

The server logs have 0 errors and 0 peer-wait timeouts in every run.

<details>
<summary>Commands</summary>

```bash
export VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER=1 VLLM_ROCM_MUSE_MOE_REDUCE_DTYPE=bf16 VLLM_USE_BREAKABLE_CUDAGRAPH=1 \
       AITER_UNIFIED_ATTN_SHORT_QUERY_3D=1 VLLM_KV_CACHE_LAYOUT=LBHNC VLLM_USE_RUST_FRONTEND=0
vllm serve amd/Muse-Spark-Open-816B-A42B-Quark-MXFP4 \
  --tensor-parallel-size 8 --enable-expert-parallel \
  --reasoning-parser muse --enable-auto-tool-choice --tool-call-parser muse \
  --dtype bfloat16 --distributed-executor-backend mp --language-model-only \
  --compilation-config '{"cudagraph_mode":"FULL_AND_PIECEWISE"}' \
  --disable-prefix-caching --enable-chunked-prefill --attention-backend ROCM_AITER_FA \
  --max-model-len 1048576 --max-num-seqs 16 --max-num-batched-tokens 8192 --gpu-memory-utilization 0.90 \
  --speculative-config '{"method":"dspark","model":"Inferact/Muse-Spark-Open-DSpark","num_speculative_tokens":7,"draft_sample_method":"probabilistic","rejection_sample_method":"block","enable_adaptive_verification":false,"attention_backend":"ROCM_AITER_FA"}' \
  --monokernel        # stock TEP8: the same command without --monokernel; stock TP8: also without
                      # --enable-expert-parallel, and --max-num-seqs 8

# GSM8K: InferenceX gsm8k.yaml (5-shot, full set), lm-eval chat completions, temperature 0, concurrency C (1, 2, 4, 8, 16)
lm_eval --model local-chat-completions --apply_chat_template --tasks gsm8k.yaml \
  --model_args model=amd/Muse-Spark-Open-816B-A42B-Quark-MXFP4,base_url=http://127.0.0.1:8000/v1/chat/completions,num_concurrent=C,tokenized_requests=False,max_length=1048576 \
  --gen_kwargs max_tokens=16384,temperature=0,top_p=1
```

For AgentX: add `--enable-prefix-caching` and set `"rejection_sample_method":"synthetic","synthetic_acceptance_length":4.05`.
</details>

## Details

### Hook point

- `MuseSpark1xForCausalLM.process_weights_after_loading` calls `maybe_attach_mono`. This runs after the per-layer quant
  finalize, so the experts are already in their shuffled kernel layout. The call is collective over the TP group.
  `MuseSpark1xModel.mono` is `None` without `--monokernel`.
- `MuseSpark1xModel.forward`: if `mono.try_forward(...)` returns the residual stream, the stock layer loop does not
  run. Otherwise the stock loop runs as before.
- `MuseSpark1xAttention.forward` ends in a new `back` (o-norm, o-gate, o_proj), and `MuseSpark1xDecoderLayer.forward`
  in a new `after_attention`. The monokernel runs layer 1 up to the attention with the stock functions and calls these
  two at the seams. The stock path calls the same code in the same order.
- `compute_logits` and `compute_logits_local` start an asynchronous read of the kernels' health words (every 64
  steps, outside graph capture). A peer-rank wait that timed out raises there, instead of a hang.
- The model runner, the scheduler and the attention backends are not changed.

### Eligibility

- At startup (default deny; one `ValueError` with every reason, agreed over the TP CPU group): gfx950 with 256 CUs,
  the checkpoint's text config, TP8 + `--enable-expert-parallel` (linear placement, no EPLB), no PP / DP / DCP / PCP,
  DSpark with 7 draft tokens, no LoRA, sleep mode or weight transfer, no KV connector or offloading, bf16 model and KV
  cache, Quark OCP-MXFP4 W4A4 experts on AITER (shuffled weights and scales), the fused QK-norm / RoPE / KV insert,
  `ROCM_AITER_FA`.
- Every step, from rank-invariant data only (the batch shape and the attention metadata counts, because all ranks
  must take the same path). The step must be a uniform verify step of 1-16 requests x 8 tokens, in FULL CUDA graph
  or eager mode, with dense bf16 LBHNC KV caches (block size 16). All other steps run stock.

### Buckets

| rows (requests) | build | launches a layer |
|---|---|---|
| 8 (1), 16 (2) | K3, S = 8 / 16 | 1 |
| 24-32 (3-4) | HA + HM + HB, S = 32 | 3 |
| 40-128 (5-16) | HA + HM + HB, S = 64 / 96 / 128 (rows padded up; `nrows` = real rows) | 3 |

`--max-num-seqs` selects the builds that the server compiles. Weights are views of vLLM's parameters. The kernels
write KV into vLLM's pages through `slot_mapping` (padding slots are skipped). The peer buffers are plain `cudaMalloc`
memory, opened over IPC on the TP CPU group. All launch arguments are fixed pointers, so vLLM's FULL CUDA graphs
capture the launches.

### Fused verify attention (8, 16 and 32 rows)

From layer 2 on, layer i's verify attention runs at the head of K3_i / HA_i, for both the sliding-window and the full
layers. It is split over all 256 CTAs by (request, KV head, key range) and merged before o_proj. It reads the layer's
bf16 KV cache through its KV cache group's `block_table` / `seq_lens`, the impl's softmax scale, and the window
(2047, 0). Only blocks inside the window are read. The descriptor tables hold pointers and counts only. They are
keyed by their contents and written once, so captured graphs read fixed tables. If `max_model_len` is above the 1M
keys that the builds stage block ids for, vLLM's op runs. Builds of 40 rows and more keep vLLM's op.

### Numerics: a16w4, opt-in behind `--monokernel`

The kernels keep the MoE activations in bf16 (MXFP4 weights x bf16 activations). The stock path is W4A4: it
quantizes the expert inputs and the SwiGLU output to MXFP4. Thus `--monokernel` output is close to the stock output,
but not bit-identical. Prefill runs stock (W4A4). Other differences are the reduction order (fixed rank order in fp32)
and the bf16 norm multipliers. The flag help, the module README and the recipe describe this.

### Known issues

- With the DFlash2 draft (not the recipe's draft), `--monokernel` lowers the real acceptance length: AgentX c = 4
  4.83 -> 3.52. The aux-hidden-state bookkeeping is the same as in the stock loop: the new tests compare the aux
  states for the DSpark, DFlash2 and seam target layers. The cause is open (per-rank draft divergence, or a draft
  that is more sensitive to the a16w4 numerics). The recipe's DSpark draft is not affected on AgentX (2.83 vs 2.87).
- The FlyDSL cleanup keeps some unused launch arguments (the timeline and EPLB-replica pointers) and LDS slots. With
  them, every build compiles to the same code objects as the validated kernels: identical `.text` for all 30 server
  builds.
- CI cannot run the kernels: they need 8x MI355X and the checkpoint's shapes. The CI test runs the host side on one
  MI355X (below). The kernel paths were validated with the serving runs above.

### Vendored kernels

`vllm/models/muse_spark/amd/mono/kernels/` (about 6.7k lines) holds AMD's Muse Spark FlyDSL monokernel sources,
reduced to the builds that vLLM launches. They carry their MIT license header after vLLM's SPDX lines (as in
`rocm_block32_gemm.py`). They import FlyDSL and AITER's FlyDSL helpers only when the monokernel attaches. The host code
(mono/ without kernels/, model.py and two small core edits) is about 1.3k lines.

### Test plan

```bash
pytest -v -s tests/models/test_muse_spark_rocm_mono.py tests/models/test_muse_spark_logits_local.py \
  tests/models/test_muse_spark_rocm_loading.py
pre-commit run --files $(git diff --name-only origin/main)
```

- On the head e2ed1f0 (main 3d81a51): 1x MI355X: 47 passed (39 s), on the vLLM ROCm nightly image 00b6c4c with the
  Python files of this branch. Pre-commit: all hooks pass.
- `test_muse_spark_rocm_mono.py` builds a tiny real MuseSpark1x model (Quark MXFP4 experts, `ROCM_AITER_FA`, LBHNC bf16
  KV cache). It loads the model through the dummy loader + `load_weights` + `process_weights_after_loading`, and runs
  it with real attention metadata builders and bound KV caches.
  - Guards: refused before the weight finalize, accepted after it. Config and deployment guards use real vLLM
    configs.
  - Weight views alias vLLM's parameters.
  - Step tests (7 shapes x 3 aux-layer sets: the DSpark and DFlash2 drafts' layers and the stock / mono seams): the
    FlyDSL launches build only for the checkpoint's TEP8 shapes. The test runs each launch as the stock layer pieces
    that it replaces, on the device memory at the pointers that the host passes. Hidden states and the KV caches of
    all layers are bit-exact vs the stock loop. Aux hidden states match at fp32 rounding. Prefill, mixed, short-query,
    too-wide and PIECEWISE steps run stock.
  - Mutants fail these tests: aux shifted by one layer, dropped aux gather, wrong q buffer for the fused attention,
    KV written to the wrong layer, dropped stock layer-1 aux.
- The test is in the `Basic Models (Other)` step and its MI355 mirror (`models_basic.yaml`).

### Follow-ups

- Move to the RFC #60904 layout (`vllm/models/muse_spark/amd/specialized_decode/`, tests under
  `tests/models/muse_spark/`) in a separate PR.
- A TP8 numerics test on 8x MI355X: each launch vs vLLM's layer on random full-size weights, as
  `test_dsv41_mono_numerics.py` does.
- Fused attention for the 40-128-row builds (c >= 5).
- Remove the unused launch arguments and LDS slots (this changes the code objects, so it needs a new validation).
- The DFlash2 acceptance drop (known issues).

commits.pr_title: [Bugfix][ROCm] Use 64-bit row offsets in the RDNA hybrid W4A16 GEMM
commits.pr_body:
## Overview

`_triton_w4a16_skinny_fmt_kernel` indexed activations and outputs with int32 row offsets, which wrap once M × K or M × N passes 2^31: the store faults with `HSA_STATUS_ERROR_MEMORY_FAULT` and the process hangs, and the load returns mapped garbage, so 127 rows come back NaN. Same class as #63049, which #63054 fixed for the CDNA kernel; this is the gfx11/gfx12 sibling.

## Claims

- cast `pid_m` to int64, which widens both `offs_m * stride_am` and `offs_m * N`; `offs_m` is the only offset here that scales with M.

## Validation

```bash
pytest tests/kernels/quantization/test_rdna_hybrid_w4a16.py -k int32_offsets   # R9700, gfx1201
```

| (K, N), M = 2^31 // max(K, N) + 128 | main | this PR |
|---|---|---|
| (256, 34816), M=61,808 | `Fatal Python error: Aborted` on the store, then hangs | 2 passed, 0.023 max abs dev |
| (17408, 256), M=123,489 | 127 NaN rows, first at row 123,362 | 2 passed, 0 NaN rows over all M |

Manually tested on an R9700 (gfx1201): both parametrizations fail on main and pass with the change. No CI pool covers gfx11/gfx12, so the test is gated on `on_gfx1x()` like the file's other kernel tests, because `tests/kernels/quantization` runs on MI300 and MI355 and neither ships this kernel.

## Details

Test tolerance stays at the file's `rtol=1e-2, atol=5e-2`, since a K=17,408 bf16 dot accumulates differently at 64-wide BLOCK_K.

commits.pr_title: [Perf][MiniMax-M3] Sequence parallelism and GEMM-RS for TP + MegaMoE
commits.pr_body:
<!-- markdownlint-disable -->

## Overview

This PR adds sequence parallelism (SP) to MiniMax-M3 on NVIDIA when running TP + EP with the MegaMoE backend, plus the GEMM-RS kernel for `o_proj` and the dense MLP `down_proj`. The design follows the existing Kimi-K3 and DeepSeek-V4.1 SP.

Without SP, MegaMoE already shards tokens across TP ranks internally, but then writes its shard into a zero-filled full-size buffer, and the next RMSNorm all-reduces it. So every layer pays 2 full all-reduces: one after attention, and one on a mostly-zero MoE output. With SP, the residual stream stays sharded by token, and each MoE layer does 1 all-gather before attention and 1 reduce-scatter after `o_proj`. MegaMoE consumes the shard directly. The 3 dense layers do one more all-gather/reduce-scatter pair around their MLP.

## Claims

- SP is enabled automatically for TP > 1 + EP + MegaMoE + PP1, same rule as DeepSeek-V4.1 and Kimi-K3. GEMM-RS is opt-in with `VLLM_ENABLE_GEMM_RS=1`.
- On 4×GB300 with `MiniMaxAI/MiniMax-M3.1-Flash` (8k in / 1k out, DSpark spec decode), compared to TP4 + EP without SP:
  - P50 TTFT is 14-20% lower at all concurrencies.
  - Output throughput is +6.5% at concurrency 16 and +13.6% at concurrency 64, a tie at concurrency 4, and -4% at concurrency 1 (see below).
- gsm8k is unchanged.

## Validation

All benchmarks were done on a single 4×GB300 node, with `f81a414fae` as the base and `MiniMaxAI/MiniMax-M3.1-Flash` (`9e7ebac`). The serve command is the "Single node (TP4, NVIDIA GB200)" command from the [vLLM recipe](https://recipes.vllm.ai/MiniMaxAI/MiniMax-M3.1-Flash), plus `--no-enable-prefix-caching`. 3 setups are compared:

- **TP4**: the recipe command as-is, on main
- **TP4 + EP**: `-ep --moe-backend deep_gemm_mega_moe`, on main
- **TP4 + EP + SP**: same flags with `VLLM_ENABLE_GEMM_RS=1`, on this PR

<details>
<summary>Serve command (TP4 + EP + SP)</summary>

```bash
VLLM_FLOAT32_MATMUL_PRECISION=high VLLM_ENABLE_GEMM_RS=1 \
vllm serve MiniMaxAI/MiniMax-M3.1-Flash \
  -tp 4 -ep --moe-backend deep_gemm_mega_moe \
  --reasoning-parser minimax_m3 \
  --block-size 128 \
  --kv-cache-dtype nvfp4 \
  --attention-config '{"indexer_kv_dtype": "nvfp4", "use_prefill_query_quantization": true}' \
  --compilation-config '{"cudagraph_mode": "FULL_AND_PIECEWISE"}' \
  --speculative-config '{"method":"dspark","num_speculative_tokens":7,"attention_backend":"FLASHINFER_TS","kv_cache_dtype":"fp8","draft_sample_method":"probabilistic","rejection_sample_method":"block"}' \
  --max-num-seqs 256 \
  --disable-hybrid-kv-cache-manager \
  --no-enable-prefix-caching
```

</details>

### E2E: SpeedBench throughput_8k

```bash
VLLM_USE_RUST_BENCH=1 vllm bench serve --backend openai-chat \
  --dataset-name speed-bench --speed-bench-config throughput_8k \
  --speed-bench-max-input-len 8192 --speed-bench-output-len 1024 --ignore-eos \
  --num-warmups 5 --sweep-max-concurrency 1,4,16,64 --sweep-num-prompts-factor 10
```

The full sweep was run twice for each setup, restarting the server in between. Each cell is the range over the 2 runs; best (by mean) in **bold**.

**Output throughput**

| Concurrency | TP4 | TP4 + EP | TP4 + EP + SP (this PR) |
| ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| 1 | **410–411 tok/s** | 370 tok/s | 355 tok/s |
| 4 | **1,022–1,058 tok/s** | 928–950 tok/s | 945–972 tok/s |
| 16 | 2,212–2,245 tok/s | 2,254–2,260 tok/s | **2,397–2,410 tok/s** |
| 64 | 3,937–3,938 tok/s | 4,299–4,338 tok/s | **4,896–4,914 tok/s** |

**P50 TTFT**

| Concurrency | TP4 | TP4 + EP | TP4 + EP + SP (this PR) |
| ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| 1 | 164–166 ms | 140 ms | **111–114 ms** |
| 4 | 190–193 ms | 163–167 ms | **134–137 ms** |
| 16 | 200–202 ms | 179–184 ms | **151–152 ms** |
| 64 | 289–329 ms | 266–280 ms | **233–236 ms** |

**P50 TPOT**

| Concurrency | TP4 | TP4 + EP | TP4 + EP + SP (this PR) |
| ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| 1 | **2.53 ms** | 2.68 ms | 2.76 ms |
| 4 | **3.65–3.79 ms** | 4.30–4.53 ms | 3.98–4.28 ms |
| 16 | 6.55–6.64 ms | 6.52–6.81 ms | **6.12–6.68 ms** |
| 64 | 15.38–15.71 ms | 14.05–14.08 ms | **12.16–12.39 ms** |

As expected, pure TP4 is the fastest at low concurrency, and EP pulls ahead at high concurrency. SP lowers TTFT at every concurrency, with no overlap between the ranges, and widens EP's lead in throughput at concurrency 16 and 64. At concurrency 4 and for TPOT at concurrency 16, the SP and EP ranges overlap, so those are a tie.

At concurrency 1, TPOT is 3% higher with SP. This comes from spec decode acceptance (3.10 vs 3.20), not from slower steps: TPOT × acceptance length is the same (8.56 ms vs 8.58 ms). Concurrency 1 only has 10 prompts, so a small numerical difference in the outputs is enough to change the acceptance length. It was identical in both runs.

<details>
<summary>Acceptance length (mean of 2 runs)</summary>

| Concurrency | TP4 | TP4 + EP | TP4 + EP + SP (this PR) |
| ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| 1 | 3.02 | 3.20 | 3.10 |
| 4 | 3.08 | 3.11 | 3.09 |
| 16 | 3.14 | 3.15 | 3.17 |
| 64 | 3.15 | 3.14 | 3.16 |

</details>

### Accuracy

gsm8k, 5-shot, chat completions, temperature 0. One eval per server start (run 1 / run 2).

| Metric | TP4 | TP4 + EP | TP4 + EP + SP (this PR) |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| flexible-extract | 95.53 / 95.75 | 95.45 / 95.98 | 96.13 / 95.45 |
| strict-match | 95.00 / 95.45 | 95.22 / 95.68 | 95.91 / 95.22 |

### GEMM-RS microbenchmark

```bash
torchrun --nproc-per-node=4 -- benchmarks/kernels/benchmark_gemm_rs_ar.py \
  --model minimax_m3 --backend flashinfer_cutedsl \
  --m 128 512 768 1024 1152 1280 1536 2048 4096 8192 16384 32768
```

TP4, N=6144. Baseline is the existing unfused path in vLLM (MXFP8 GEMM + `sp_reduce_scatter`).

| M | o_proj (K=2048) baseline | o_proj GEMM-RS | down_proj (K=3072) baseline | down_proj GEMM-RS |
|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| 128 | 36.6 us | 39.8 us (0.92x) | 55.9 us | 60.5 us (0.92x) |
| 512 | 61.8 us | 63.3 us (0.98x) | 64.6 us | 64.9 us (1.00x) |
| 768 | 68.2 us | 67.4 us (1.01x) | 68.7 us | 66.7 us (1.03x) |
| 1024 | 79.0 us | 76.9 us (1.03x) | 79.0 us | 72.9 us (1.08x) |
| 1536 | 101.5 us | 84.0 us (1.21x) | 105.3 us | 82.2 us (1.28x) |
| 2048 | 114.1 us | 90.9 us (1.26x) | 119.4 us | 89.2 us (1.34x) |
| 4096 | 179.3 us | 133.7 us (1.34x) | 191.6 us | 129.9 us (1.47x) |
| 8192 | 271.3 us | 211.6 us (1.28x) | 299.7 us | 210.0 us (1.43x) |
| 16384 | 475.0 us | 363.6 us (1.31x) | 558.9 us | 374.4 us (1.49x) |
| 32768 | 952.6 us | 680.1 us (1.40x) | 1146.9 us | 704.8 us (1.63x) |

M=512-1536 was repeated two more times. GEMM-RS was faster at M ≥ 1024 every time, while M=768 was mixed, so GEMM-RS is only used for M ≥ 1024.

Above 1024 tokens, the fused dense GEMM1 hands `down_proj` an MXFP8 `QuantizedActivation`, so the BF16-input numbers above include an activation quantization that production skips. Re-measured with the same pre-quantized input for both paths (range over 2 runs):

| M | down_proj (K=3072) baseline | down_proj GEMM-RS |
|---:|---:|---:|
| 1152 | 66.4–74.4 us | 61.4–66.2 us (1.08–1.12x) |
| 1280 | 72.8–74.9 us | 63.6–65.7 us (1.14x) |
| 1536 | 88.9–91.4 us | 65.1–66.7 us (1.37x) |
| 2048 | 109.7–110.3 us | 76.9–78.2 us (1.41–1.43x) |
| 4096 | 173.8–175.8 us | 111.3–114.0 us (1.54–1.56x) |
| 8192 | 279.4–279.7 us | 190.6–192.1 us (1.45–1.47x) |
| 16384 | 534.0–534.7 us | 343.3–345.2 us (1.55–1.56x) |
| 32768 | 1083.8–1087.4 us | 650.4–652.4 us (1.66–1.67x) |

GEMM-RS stays faster at every M above the threshold.

### Tests

- `tests/kernels/test_gemm_rs_ar.py`: extended with a pre-quantized MXFP8 input for both MXFP8 backends. Passes on 2×GB300. CI runs it in the 2×B200 distributed step.
- E2E SP needs 4 SM100 GPUs in one NVLink domain plus the M3.1 checkpoint, which CI does not have. It is covered by the benchmark and gsm8k runs above.

## Details

Changes in `vllm/models/minimax_m3/nvidia/model.py`:
- **Model forward**: shard the hidden states after the embedding, and shard the MegaMoE padding mask once. At the end, all-gather the output together with the EAGLE3/DSpark aux hidden states in 1 collective.
- **Attention**: all-gather the input, reduce-scatter the output (`o_proj` + `sp_reduce_scatter`, or GEMM-RS).
- **MegaMoE**: takes the shard as-is (`input_is_sequence_sharded`), so no shard/gather/zero-fill. The existing `use_sequence_parallel` flag in `MiniMaxM3MoE` is renamed to `shard_replicated_input`, since it means the opposite of model-level SP.
- **Dense MLP** (3 of 60 layers): all-gather, `gate_up` (keeps the fused dense GEMM1) and `down_proj`, then reduce-scatter.
- **Fusions**: the AR + Gemma RMSNorm fusions are skipped under SP, since there is nothing left to all-reduce.

**GEMM-RS with a quantized input** Above its token threshold, the fused dense GEMM1 outputs an MXFP8 `QuantizedActivation` instead of BF16. So `GemmRsAr.apply()` now accepts it and skips its own quantization. The scales are already in the F8_128x4 swizzled layout that the kernel expects.

**Limitations and follow-ups**
- MTP blocks and PP > 1 don't use SP.
- The dense MLP stays TP-sharded instead of adding Kimi-K3's replicated option, since it is only 3 layers.
- The all-gathers move BF16. Gathering the MXFP8 `qkv_proj` input instead would halve the bytes; this is left for a follow-up.

AI assistance (Claude) was used to write this change and to run the validation above.

commits.pr_title: [Bugfix][EC Connector] Allocate producer control ports at startup
commits.pr_body:
## Overview

Avoid NIXL EC producer control-port collisions when multiple instances or DP replicas share a host, while retaining explicit endpoint configuration.

## Claims

- Allocate an OS-assigned port by default and advertise the actual bound port through `ec_transfer_params.peer_port`.
- Keep `VLLM_EC_SIDE_CHANNEL_HOST` and `VLLM_EC_SIDE_CHANNEL_PORT` overrides. A nonzero port uses `base_port + data_parallel_index`; `0` remains automatic.
- Preserve `ec_transfer_config.engine_id` in the NIXL agent name and append the DP index to distinguish replicas.

## Validation

<details>
<summary>Transport and configuration validation</summary>

```bash
.venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/v1/ec_connector/unit/test_{control,data,session,scheduler_nixl_ctor,scheduler_nixl_producer,scheduler_nixl_consumer}.py -q
```

112 passed, including real ZMQ request/reply and NIXL peer registration. The updated tests reproduce ignored endpoint overrides and engine IDs before the fix. GPU serving was not rerun for this revision.

</details>

## Details

Bind port `0` directly on the serving socket and read `LAST_ENDPOINT`, avoiding a separate port-reservation race. The host defaults to `get_ip()` (honoring `VLLM_HOST_IP`); set `VLLM_EC_SIDE_CHANNEL_HOST=localhost` for loopback-only binding. Wildcard addresses are rejected because peers need a reachable address.

Fixed-port conflicts fail startup rather than silently choosing another port. Independent instances using fixed ports must use non-overlapping ranges; consumers use the advertised endpoint without matching port configuration.

No equivalent open fix was found in the EC control-port search.

commits.pr_title: [Bugfix][Tool Parser] Parse bare FunctionGemma arguments and stream them as valid JSON
commits.pr_body:
## Overview

Fix the `functiongemma` tool parser dropping every non-string argument, and make its streamed arguments reassemble into valid JSON. Fixes #63983.

## Claims

- Bare booleans, numbers, `null`, arrays and objects are parsed in streaming and non-streaming, nested containers included.
- Streamed deltas of a multi-argument call concatenate to one JSON object.
- A streamed call still gets closed when its end tag shares a delta with the next call's start tag.
- A streamed call with no arguments sends `{}` instead of an empty string.

## Validation

```bash
pytest tests/tool_parsers/test_functiongemma_tool_parser.py
pytest tests/entrypoints/tool_parsers/test_functiongemma_tool_parser.py
```

| Parser | parser tests (CPU) | server tests (H200) |
| --- | --- | --- |
| main (`eb703fbb3d`) | 25 failed, 17 passed | 3 failed, 4 passed |
| previous head (`fa086599ec`) | 5 failed, 37 passed | 4 failed, 3 passed |
| this PR | 42 passed | 7 passed |

The server tests pin the model output with a `structured_outputs` regex, so they cover serving and parsing rather than what the model decides to call. pre-commit passes on the changed files. Existing Buildkite steps select both test files, but CI has not run on this PR yet.

### End-to-end (vllm serve, real model)

`unsloth/functiongemma-270m-it` (ungated mirror of `google/functiongemma-270m-it`, same `chat_template.jinja`) on one shared H200, through the OpenAI client with `tool_choice="auto"` and `temperature=0`. Streamed `tool_calls` deltas are concatenated per index, as a client would.

```bash
VLLM_USE_FLASHINFER_SAMPLER=0 vllm serve unsloth/functiongemma-270m-it \
  --tool-call-parser functiongemma --enable-auto-tool-choice \
  --max-model-len 2048 --gpu-memory-utilization 0.04 --enforce-eager --max-num-seqs 4
```

Raw model output for the `set_alarm` request (`/v1/completions`, `skip_special_tokens=false`):

```text
<start_function_call>call:set_alarm{days:[<escape>mon<escape>,<escape>tue<escape>],enabled:true,hour:7,label:<escape>Wake up<escape>}<end_function_call>
```

| Request | main | this PR |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `set_alarm` (int, bool, array, string), non-streaming | `{"label": "Wake up"}` | `{"days": ["mon", "tue"], "enabled": true, "hour": 7, "label": "Wake up"}` |
| `set_alarm`, streaming | `{"label": "Wake up"}` | `{"days": ["mon", "tue"], "enabled": true, "hour": 7, "label": "Wake up"}` |
| `get_weather` (two strings), non-streaming | `{"city": "San Francisco", "unit": "celsius"}` | same |
| `get_weather`, streaming | `{"city": "San Francisco"} "unit": "celsius"}` (invalid JSON) | `{"city": "San Francisco", "unit": "celsius"}` |

Review fixes, streaming, same server. The two-call rows pin the output with a regex and set `stream_interval` per request to merge deltas:

| Request | previous head (`fa086599ec`) | this PR |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `get_current_time` (no parameters), real model output | `''` | `{}` |
| Two calls, `stream_interval=4`, delta is `<end_function_call><start_function_call>call:` | `{"city": "Paris"` (invalid JSON) | `{"city": "Paris"}` |
| Two calls, `stream_interval=8`, first call's arguments are in that delta too | `''` | `{"city": "Paris"}` |

Every `stream_interval` from 1 to 6, and 8, gives both calls with valid JSON on this PR.

Screenshots, client script and server logs from the first run (`fa086599ec`): [branch `e2e-evidence-63992`](https://github.com/saifltr/vllm/tree/e2e-evidence-63992/e2e_evidence).

<details>
<summary>client</summary>

```python
TOOLS = [{"type": "function", "function": {"name": "set_alarm", "parameters": {"type": "object", "properties": {
    "hour": {"type": "integer"}, "enabled": {"type": "boolean"}, "label": {"type": "string"},
    "days": {"type": "array", "items": {"type": "string"}}}, "required": ["hour", "enabled", "label", "days"]}}}]
PROMPT = "Set an alarm for 7 o'clock labeled Wake up, enabled, on mon and tue."
WEATHER_TOOLS = [{"type": "function", "function": {"name": "get_weather", "parameters": {"type": "object", "properties": {
    "city": {"type": "string"}, "unit": {"type": "string", "enum": ["celsius", "fahrenheit"]}}, "required": ["city", "unit"]}}}]
WEATHER_PROMPT = "What's the weather in San Francisco in celsius?"
NO_ARG_TOOLS = [{"type": "function", "function": {"name": "get_current_time", "parameters": {"type": "object", "properties": {}}}}]
NO_ARG_PROMPT = "What time is it right now?"
# client.chat.completions.create(model=..., messages=[{"role": "user", "content": PROMPT}], tools=TOOLS,
#                                tool_choice="auto", temperature=0, max_tokens=128, stream=stream)
```

</details>

## Details

The template's `format_argument` macro wraps only strings in `<escape>`, e.g. `enabled:true,hour:7,days:[<escape>mon<escape>],snooze:{minutes:5}`. The old `arg_regex` only matched `key:<escape>...<escape>`, so bare values were dropped. A small recursive parser for that grammar replaces it. With `partial=True` (streaming) it stops at the first incomplete value, so each value is streamed once in its final form. A bare word that is not a JSON literal stays a string.

Streaming diffs are computed by length against `json.dumps(args)`, so the closing brace is held back until the call ends. That left two gaps, both fixed here. When an end tag and the next start tag arrive together, the start branch returned before closing the earlier call, so it never got its brace, or any arguments if they were still unsent. A call with no arguments streamed nothing because the end branch skipped empty arguments. Both paths now go through `_close_tool_call`. Deltas can merge when the client falls behind the engine or `stream_interval` is above 1.

Known limitation: from `stream_interval=10` in these runs, a call's name can share a delta with its end tag, and the name is lost. At 64 the second call is lost too. main behaves the same or worse here, so this is left for a follow-up.

Related PRs:

- #63947 fixes #63906, a separate bug. `<escape>` values keep their current decoding here, so `<escape>123<escape>` is still the integer 123.
- #48705 fixes the brace issue the same way. It is included here because the streaming tests cannot reassemble a multi-argument call without it. Happy to rebase if #48705 lands first.
- #64360 targets the same issue and was opened a day after this PR.

commits.pr_title: [Core] Extensible KV cache
commits.pr_body:
## Overview

Size the KV cache from the GPU memory actually free after CUDA graph capture and warmup, instead of from a pre-capture profiling estimate. The cache's address range is reserved up front with the driver's virtual memory API, and physical memory is mapped into it only once the final size is known. Enabled by default on CUDA and ROCm with the V2 model runner.

Productization of @zhuohan123's demonstration in #47363; replaces #50779.

### Background

The KV cache has to exist before CUDA graph capture, because captured graphs bake in its addresses. So today it is sized from a profiling run that happens before capture and warmup, and everything allocated after that has to be guessed:
- **CUDA graph memory** is either ignored or estimated with a throwaway capture pass, which costs startup time.
- **Warmup and runtime transients** that profiling doesn't exercise, such as attention workspaces, sampler and logprobs buffers, and spec-decode drafts, are covered only by slack.

That slack is the `gpu_memory_utilization=0.92` default: 8% of the device, about 15 GiB of a 192 GiB GPU, left idle to absorb estimation error. When the estimate is too optimistic, the engine runs out of memory at runtime anyway.

### Extensible KV cache

The full KV cache capacity is reserved as virtual address space, with no physical memory behind it. Only the blocks that capture and warmup actually touch are backed with physical pages. After warmup, each worker measures the memory that is really free and the transient peaks it really saw. The engine then commits the final block count in one step, by mapping more physical memory into the same reserved range.

Addresses never move, so the layer views and the already-captured CUDA graphs stay valid. The cache is sized from measurement rather than from an estimate, so the default can use the whole device, keeping a measured transient reserve plus a margin.

## Claims

- **Larger KV cache by default:** 4–10% more KV cache tokens (4.9–11.3 GiB per GPU) across eight models on GB200, most of them 7–10%. The gain comes from no longer needing the 8% slack. At an explicit `gpu_memory_utilization=0.92`, the cache comes out 1–4% *smaller* than today's. It subtracts the CUDA graph and warmup memory it actually measured, which today's path leaves the slack to absorb.
- **Faster engine startup:** no throwaway CUDA graph capture pass to estimate graph memory. Engine init time, excluding weight loading, falls 21–34% (5–34 s); end-to-end startup falls 6–18%.
- **No tuning `gpu_memory_utilization` to avoid OOMs:** the cache size follows what the model, graphs and warmup actually use. The utilization setting remains a cap for sharing a GPU.
- Works with sleep mode, CUDA graphs, spec decode, hybrid models, TP/PP/DP, and the KV connectors listed under "Compatibility". Where a configuration can't use it, it falls back to today's estimate-based sizing automatically. An explicit `--enable-extensible-kv-cache` there is an error.

## Validation

- Capacity and startup benchmarks: see "Results" below.
- Unit tests:
  - `tests/utils_/test_extensible_tensor.py`
  - `tests/utils_/test_vmm_driver.py`
  - `tests/v1/worker/test_extensible_kv_cache.py`
  - `tests/v1/core/test_kv_cache_planning.py`
  - `tests/v1/engine/test_engine_args.py`
  - `tests/v1/worker/test_gpu_worker.py`
- End-to-end: greedy outputs match with the feature on and off, and before and after sleep/wake.
- NIXL P/D accuracy on GB200; on ROCm, with patched UCX and ROCr (see "Compatibility").

## Results

GB200 (189 GiB per GPU), default settings otherwise. Each start is a fresh process.
- **Variants:**
  - **off:** `--no-enable-extensible-kv-cache`, i.e. today's sizing with the default `gpu_memory_utilization=0.92`.
  - **on:** this PR's defaults.
- **Method:**
  - One unmeasured warm-up start per variant, to populate the torch.compile, JIT and weight page caches.
  - Then three interleaved off/on pairs; medians are reported.
  - Weights load from a warm page cache, so end-to-end times are faster than a cold start. Weight loading is identical between variants.

**KV cache capacity per GPU**

| Model | TP | off | on | Gain | Tokens | on, at 0.92 |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Qwen3-8B | 1 | 150.2 GiB | 161.6 GiB | +11.3 GiB | +7.5% | −0.6% |
| Qwen3-8B + EAGLE3 | 1 | 147.3 GiB | 157.4 GiB | +10.1 GiB | +6.8% | −1.4% |
| Qwen3-32B | 1 | 103.1 GiB | 113.0 GiB | +9.9 GiB | +9.5% | −1.9% |
| gpt-oss-20b | 1 | 150.5 GiB | 161.0 GiB | +10.5 GiB | +7.0% | −0.9% |
| Qwen3.6-35B-A3B | 1 | 97.6 GiB | 106.2 GiB | +8.6 GiB | +8.8% | −2.3% |
| MiniMax-M2.7 | 4 | 109.7 GiB | 118.4 GiB | +8.7 GiB | +7.9% | −1.3% |
| Qwen3-235B-A22B-FP8 | 4 | 108.1 GiB | 117.1 GiB | +9.0 GiB | +8.2% | −1.5% |
| DeepSeek-V4-Flash | 4 | 119.9 GiB | 124.9 GiB | +4.9 GiB | +4.1% | −3.7% |

- **"on, at 0.92"** is the extensible cache at an explicit `gpu_memory_utilization=0.92`, compared with off. The cache comes out slightly smaller there because it subtracts the CUDA graph and warmup memory it measured, which today's sizing leaves to the slack.
- **DeepSeek-V4-Flash gains least** because its CUDA graphs and workspaces need about 15 GiB per GPU after warmup. Today's sizing leaves almost all of that to the 8% slack, so the slack was mostly in use already.

**Startup time** (median of 3)

| Model | TP | Engine init, off | Engine init, on | Change | End-to-end, off | End-to-end, on | Change |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Qwen3-8B | 1 | 17.7 s | 12.5 s | −5.2 s (−29%) | 50.0 s | 40.9 s | −9.1 s (−18%) |
| Qwen3-8B + EAGLE3 | 1 | 20.1 s | 13.7 s | −6.3 s (−32%) | 51.7 s | 44.7 s | −7.0 s (−14%) |
| Qwen3-32B | 1 | 30.7 s | 21.6 s | −9.1 s (−30%) | 80.9 s | 71.4 s | −9.5 s (−12%) |
| gpt-oss-20b | 1 | 19.2 s | 13.8 s | −5.3 s (−28%) | 47.2 s | 42.2 s | −5.0 s (−11%) |
| Qwen3.6-35B-A3B | 1 | 53.3 s | 42.4 s | −11.0 s (−21%) | 119.7 s | 109.4 s | −10.4 s (−9%) |
| MiniMax-M2.7 | 4 | 55.9 s | 38.3 s | −17.6 s (−31%) | 146.9 s | 137.4 s | −9.4 s (−6%) |
| Qwen3-235B-A22B-FP8 | 4 | 76.1 s | 50.1 s | −26.0 s (−34%) | 173.8 s | 144.2 s | −29.6 s (−17%) |
| DeepSeek-V4-Flash | 4 | 112.2 s | 77.9 s | −34.2 s (−30%) | 192.2 s | 174.2 s | −18.0 s (−9%) |

- **Engine init** is the logged "init engine (profile, create kv cache, warmup model)" time, which excludes weight loading.
- **End-to-end** runs from process start until `LLM()` returns.
- **Spread:** engine init varied by about 1–2 s within a variant, and every on start was faster than every off start.
- **Where the time goes:** most of the saving is the throwaway CUDA graph capture pass that today's sizing runs to estimate graph memory. The actual capture takes the same time in both variants.
- **TP4 runs loaded checkpoints lazily** (`safetensors_load_strategy="lazy"`). The automatic background prefetch from Lustre intermittently hung multi-rank loading, independently of this change. MiniMax-M2.7's off starts used the prefetch, so its end-to-end comparison mixes the two loading modes.

<!-- TODO: H200 -->

## Details

### Implementation

- **`ExtensibleTensor`** (`vllm/utils/extensible_tensor.py`, `vllm/utils/vmm_driver.py`):
  - A tensor over a reserved virtual address range, exposed to torch through DLPack.
  - Its segments are backed with physical memory on demand, in driver-granule chunks; newly committed blocks are zeroed.
  - Uses the CUDA (`cuMem*`) and HIP (`hipMem*`) VMM APIs through ctypes.
  - A startup probe falls back to estimate-based sizing where the driver lacks VMM support, or where a HIP runtime has the `hipMemSetAccess` defect.
- **`ExtensibleKVCache`** (`vllm/v1/worker/extensible_kv_cache.py`):
  - Plugs into `allocate_kv_cache` as an allocator hook. It reserves the capacity from the profiled budget and splits it into per-layer (or per-tensor) segments, so kernels and layer views are unchanged.
  - Before capture, only the null block is backed. Warmup commits the blocks it addresses.
- **Sizing** (`gpu_worker._measure_kv_cache_blocks`, `kv_cache_planning.finalize_extensible_kv_cache`):
  - After warmup, each worker reports how many blocks fit. That is its budget less two things:
    - the measured transient peak: the larger of the profiling peak and the warmup peak;
    - a margin of `max(1 GiB, 0.75 × transient peak)`.
  - The engine takes the minimum across workers, and across DP engines, which step in lockstep. It then shrinks the configs and issues one `extend_kv_cache` RPC.
  - Warmup gains a full-budget prefill step and a prompt-logprobs chunk, so their peaks are measured rather than estimated. For MLA models it also runs a prefill over one chunked-context workspace of cached context, which measures MLA's context up-projection for prefix cache hits.
  - With the feature on and `gpu_memory_utilization` unset, the utilization defaults to 1.0; otherwise it stays 0.92. The CUDA graph memory profiling pass is skipped.
- **Sleep mode:** sleep, and `release_kv_cache_memory()`, unmap the physical pages; wake remaps them at the same addresses.
- **Weight updates** (`reload_weights`, weight-transfer sessions): a layerwise update needs transient memory that warmup can't measure, at its peak a few times the largest layer's checkpoint-format size. Before any weight changes, the worker checks free memory against that estimate:
  - If short after a pause that cleared the KV cache (the default RL weight-update flow), it releases the cache's physical memory for the update and remaps it afterwards. Nothing is reserved in normal serving.
  - Otherwise a reload fails before loading if even the largest layer can't fit, and warns if only the estimate doesn't.
- **KV connectors:**
  - The worker-side connector is created after the final extend, so it registers the final memory.
  - Under a connector, segment boundaries are aligned to the driver granule, so RDMA registrations never span physical chunks.
- **Consistency:** every worker and every DP engine agrees on whether the feature is on and on the warmup block count, so they warm up the same steps.

### Compatibility

| Not supported | Behavior | What enabling it would need |
|---|---|---|
| Platforms other than CUDA/ROCm | Off | A `VmmDriver` per platform. XPU looks feasible: Level Zero has all the VMM primitives, but the calls need PyTorch's SYCL context (a small C++ op), and PyTorch's XPU DLPack import would need to accept the mapped pointer. |
| V1 model runner | Off | Only the V2 runner is wired up. Not planned, since V1 is deprecated. |
| `kv_cache_memory_bytes`, `num_gpu_blocks_override` | Off; error if requested | Nothing: an explicit size makes measured sizing moot. |
| HiSparse | Off | HiSparse allocates its own KV cache. It would need to allocate through the extensible allocator hook. |
| Elastic EP | Off | Scale-up launches skip warmup and reuse the profiled size. New ranks would need to adopt the running engines' committed block count. |
| `LMCacheMPConnector` | Off | It shares the cache through legacy CUDA IPC, which can't export VMM memory. Needs POSIX-fd exportable allocations, LMCache's VMM IPC wrapper (`VmmCudaIPCWrapper` / `resolve_kv_wrapper_factory`) in `wrap_kv_caches`, and handling of tensors that span segments. |
| Connectors with `custom_mem_pool` (Mooncake NVLink/BAREX) | Off | The cache must come from the connector's pool. The pool would need to supply physical allocations that can be mapped into the reserved range. |
| ROCm with NIXL, Mooncake or MoRIIO | Off | UCX and ROCr can't yet register or share HIP VMM memory. Fixed upstream in openucx/ucx#12137–#12140 and ROCm/rocm-systems#13989. Once those reach the ROCm image, drop the gate and allocate exportable (POSIX-fd) memory, which is ready in a follow-up commit. |
| HIP runtimes before TheRock 7.12 | Off (probed) | Fixed upstream by ROCm/rocm-systems#2451. Nothing needed on the vLLM side. |
| Models without a KV cache | Off | Nothing to size. |
| Weight reloads without a cache-clearing pause (e.g. `reload_weights` called directly while serving) | On; the reload needs headroom from `gpu_memory_utilization`. Without it the reload warns and may run out of memory, or fails before loading when even the largest layer can't fit | Release only the cache blocks that are free: commit in finer physical chunks, and have the scheduler set aside a range of free block ids for the reload. Chunked MoE weight processing would also shrink what a reload needs. |

---

Claude was used extensively to help with this.

commits.pr_body:
## Overview

This PR makes two register-pressure fixes in the DeepSeek-V4.1 mono decode K2 (`--monokernel`) at TP4 on MI355X (gfx950), for both the target and the DSpark draft. It is bit-exact and adds no env var. The code change is +16/-1 lines in 2 files, plus one compile-only test, on main e5196e2959. It builds on #60397 and overlaps #63027 (TP2).

## Claims

- **Step time (measured on main):** c1 -51 us (-0.9%), c2 -235 us (-3.5%), TP4 with DSpark k=6, over 4 ABBA rounds. At both, every PR server ran faster than every main server. The profiler puts the saving in K2 (target and draft); K1 is unchanged.
- **Bit-exact (measured):** per-rank output hashes of K1, K2 and the FFN launch equal main's at 257 TP4 configs (every width from 1 to 48, ratios 0/1/2, index sources, the DSpark draft). GSM8K-1319 is within one pass's standard error of main's, and acceptance length does not move (main 3.576, this PR 3.579, at 2 requests in flight).
- **Compile-level (measured):** at 1-16 rows the target TP4 K2 uses 230-248 VGPRs (main: 246-256) and the draft's 161-181 (main: 166-207); neither spills. On main, 14-16 rows spill, and 13 rows at an index source. Serial X8 copy chains drop from 23-25 to 3-4. Past 16 rows only the base loads move in the source, and no width spills on either tree. TP2, TP8, every K1, the FFN launch and gfx942 are binary-identical to main's.

## Validation

GPU runs used one 8x MI355X node and two images (plus `pr` with the one-line mutant below, for the negative controls): `main` = `vllm/vllm-openai-rocm:nightly-rocm100-3966924d56` with the mono-path files of main f97a8d6647 overlaid (#64008, #63816 and #64101 are newer than the nightly), and `pr` = `main` + this PR's 2 files (0a44cb7166; the head 02c9253428 only adds the `push_bases` default in `moe_context()`, and its builds are byte-identical at the 10 configs compared; main has no mono changes between f97a8d6647 and e5196e2959). Both have vLLM 0.33.0rc1.dev229, AITER 0.1.26, FlyDSL 0.4.0 and torch 2.13.0+rocm10.0.0.

- [x] `pytest -v tests/models/test_dsv41_mono_{numerics,layers,decode}.py` on MI355X with this PR: `test_mono_decode_layer_matches_vllm[2|4|8]` (6- and 48-row steps, then 300 graph replays), layers `[2-8]`, `[4-8]`, `[8-8]`, `[8-28]` and the 76 decode tests pass. `[4-42]` and the gfx942 test skip, as on main. Main's image passes the same tests, except the new one.
- [x] The new compile-only `test_mono_decode_k2_tp4_no_scratch` (TP4 K2 at 14 rows) fails on main (6 `scratch_` ops) and passes with this PR, under pytest on MI355X. It catches a revert of the late base load (255 VGPR, 4 spilled again), not a revert of the batched copies alone (250 VGPR, no spill). `test_mono_decode_layer_matches_vllm[4]` covers the copies at runtime: a one-line mutant of the batched copy, which fills the last row's last 16-byte quad with the quad before it, fails its 6-row case.
- [x] Per-rank output hashes vs main at TP4: 257 configs (target ratios 0/1/2 and the draft at every width from 1 to 48; index sources at 1-16, 21, 28 and 48 rows; padded and fold-off steps; the FFN launch), 3 reps each on each of the 4 ranks. Main and this PR are equal on 1028 of 1028 (config, rank) pairs (41,868 tensor-hash comparisons), and both are deterministic. The mutant above changes only the last row of K2's MoE output, on every rank, at all 5 of its configs of up to 16 rows, and nothing at 21 or 28 rows or in the FFN launch, so the check sees a one-quad error.
- [x] c1/c2 ABBA on main, plus c4 (Performance).
- [x] GSM8K-1319 and AL with this PR alone (Accuracy).
- [x] 553 configs per tree (505 gfx950, 48 gfx942) compiled and compared with main's builds (table under Details). The three 48-row gfx942 K2 configs fail on both trees, since gfx942 caps decode at 42 rows. `pre-commit` (ruff, mypy) passes.

**Performance.** Setup: two TP4 servers at a time, one per GPU half, one per arm. 4 rounds with the halves swapped (main|pr, pr|main, pr|main, main|pr). Each server ran a warm-up, then 3 runs x 32 prompts per concurrency. TP4 mono, DSpark k=6, adaptive verification off, random 32k/1k, synthetic acceptance length 3.87, step = ITL p50. Delta = the mean of the two same-half deltas.

| | c1 (7 rows) | c2 (14 rows) | c4 (28 rows) |
|---|---|---|---|
| main, mean of 4 servers | 5.443 ms | 6.707 ms | 8.685 ms |
| this PR, mean of 4 servers | 5.392 ms | 6.472 ms | 8.618 ms |
| delta | **-51 us (-0.9%)** | **-235 us (-3.5%)** | -67 us (-0.8%) |
| delta per round | -62, -34, -73, -35 us | -257, -198, -251, -233 us | -37, -79, -55, -98 us |
| servers, main / this PR | 5.429-5.459 / 5.377-5.402 | 6.669-6.722 / 6.464-6.484 | 8.656-8.727 / 8.610-8.628 |

Rows are target rows per step; the draft runs 6, 12 and 24. At c4 the copies are not batched and nothing spills on main, so only the base loads move. This PR is faster in every round (-37 to -98 us), but I did not profile it. An earlier single unswapped run on a stack image (nightly 83c078d955 + 5 PRs) gave c1 -59 us and c2 -256 us.

Profiler (attribution, not the measurement): GPU time of the mono launches per decode step, mean over the 4 ranks, then over the two accuracy rounds (halves swapped). The traced windows are short: 2 prompts at c1 and 4 at c2, 32k/256.

| per decode step | 7 rows | 14 rows |
|---|---|---|
| target K2 (40 launches) | -78 us (-2.7%) | -224 us (-6.0%) |
| draft K2 (3 launches) | -6 us (-3.4%) | -12 us (-5.8%) |
| target and draft K1 | within 0.2%, inside A/A noise | within 0.2%, inside A/A noise |
| all 86 mono launches | -86 us (-2.2%) | -238 us (-4.8%) |

**Accuracy.** Same images, block rejection (real acceptance), 2 rounds with the halves swapped. GSM8K-1319, 8-shot, greedy. With 2 requests in flight, every decode step takes this PR's one-tile path (7-14 target / 6-12 draft rows). With 8 in flight, 97% of the samples had 7 or more requests running, which is past the 48-row mono limit for the target, so those passes mostly check the rest of the stack.

| requests in flight | passes per arm | GSM8K, main / this PR | AL, main / this PR | questions that flip: main vs PR (main vs main, PR vs PR) |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 2 | 4 | 0.9181 / 0.9143 (-0.0038) | 3.576 / 3.579 | 68.5 (66.0, 71.3) |
| 8 | 6 | 0.9169 / 0.9138 (-0.0030) | 3.572 / 3.573 | 71.4 (72.3, 72.0) |

One pass's binomial standard error at n=1319 and 91.5% is 0.0077. Flips are the mean over pairs of passes; between arms they match the flips between two passes of the same arm.

<details>
<summary>Reproduction</summary>

```bash

VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER=1 VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER_MOE=1 VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER_TRITON_SPARSE_MLA=True \
VLLM_USE_BREAKABLE_CUDAGRAPH=1 VLLM_USE_RUST_FRONTEND=1 OMP_NUM_THREADS=1 \
vllm serve deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash --tensor-parallel-size 4 --monokernel --moe-backend aiter \
  --tokenizer-mode deepseek_v41 --language-model-only --block-size 128 --gpu-memory-utilization 0.9 \
  --max-model-len 1048576 --max-num-batched-tokens 16384 --max-num-seqs 256 --max-cudagraph-capture-size 1024 \
  --attention-config '{"indexer_kv_dtype":"mxfp4","indexer_sparse_logits":true}' \
  --engram-config '{"cpu_offload":false}' \
  --tool-call-parser deepseek_v41 --reasoning-parser deepseek_v41 --enable-auto-tool-choice \
  --speculative-config '{"method":"dspark","num_speculative_tokens":6,"draft_sample_method":"probabilistic","rejection_sample_method":"synthetic","synthetic_acceptance_length":3.87,"enable_adaptive_verification":false}'

# warm-up
vllm bench serve --backend openai --model deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash --tokenizer-mode deepseek_v41 \
  --dataset-name random --random-input-len 32768 --random-output-len 256 --ignore-eos \
  --max-concurrency 2 --num-prompts 4 --seed 7

# step time = ITL p50; 3 runs per concurrency
for c in 1 2 4; do
  vllm bench serve --backend openai --model deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash --tokenizer-mode deepseek_v41 \
    --dataset-name random --random-input-len 32768 --random-output-len 1024 --ignore-eos \
    --max-concurrency $c --num-prompts 32 --seed $((100 + c)) --percentile-metrics itl --metric-percentiles 50
done
```

Accuracy: the same server with `"rejection_sample_method":"block"` and no synthetic acceptance. GSM8K test set, 1319 questions, 8-shot, temperature 0, max 512 tokens, over `/v1/completions`, with sglang `few_shot_gsm8k`'s prompt and scoring, at 2 or 8 requests in flight. Each round's first pass is cold; every later pass uses a per-request cache salt. Acceptance length = 1 + accepted / drafts, from `/metrics` around each pass. The profiler ran on these servers (`--profiler-config '{"profiler":"torch",...}'`).

Hashes: a test that is not part of this PR runs each config eagerly 3 times on every rank, with main's `test_dsv41_mono_numerics` builders (seeded random weights in the checkpoint's formats), and hashes every K1, K2 and FFN-launch output tensor. Both images run the same test file.
</details>

## Details

**Root cause.**
1. *X8 copies.* At one token tile (up to 16 rows, covering c1 and c2 at k=6), `load_x8_rows` issues one 16-byte load per branch. Each load waits (`s_waitcnt vmcnt(0)`) before its LDS store. With this PR it issues every load first, then the masked stores. The row count is a Python int on these paths.
2. *Peer bases.* K2 loads the four peer bases at its start (`peer_bases`, #60397) and holds them to the MoE all-reduce push. At 14-16 rows (13 at an index source) K2 spills 2-4 VGPRs. At 14 and 16 rows the push reloads the bases: each reload is followed by `s_waitcnt vmcnt(0)` (4 between peer stores), which on gfx950 also waits for earlier system-scope stores, so each peer's push waits for the previous ones. At 15 rows and the 13-row index source, 2 VGPRs spill with no wait between peer stores. `stage_down` now loads the bases right before its barrier, and they still land before the first push.

**Gate.** `build_mono_k2` passes a `push_bases` callable to `run_ffn`, which puts it in the MoE context only at `tp == 4`. That one entry enables both halves. `load_x8_rows` takes the batched path only when it is set, not on gfx942, and only when the row count is a Python int (one token tile). `stage_down` rebinds `peer_addr` to the bases it loads late; gfx942 returns through `stage_down_942` before that line. The FFN launch and K1 never get the entry. TP2 is excluded: its K2 does not spill on main (70 builds, including ratio 2 at every width from 1 to 48), neither half was measured at TP2, and #63027 tunes TP2 ratio 2 with its own batched copy. TP8 is #64153.

**Tradeoffs and limitations.**
- SGPR lane spills: at 7 rows (the c1 width), target builds go 103 → 174 `v_writelane` (32 in loops, main 0) and index sources 93-105 → 68. At 14 rows (c2), target builds go 75-79 → 82 and index sources 85 → 78, none in loops. Across target and index-source builds, loop-resident `v_writelane` rises on 21 of 88 at 1-16 rows (falls on none) and on 15 of 162 past 16 rows (falls on 100). The c1, c2 and c4 measurements include these builds.
- The DSpark draft K2 at 5 rows (not a k=6 width) goes 166 → 180 VGPR, the only build at 1-16 rows that uses more VGPRs; its `v_writelane` falls 219 → 63. Past 16 rows the draft gains 1 VGPR at 16 widths, without VGPR spills, and its loop-resident `v_writelane` rises at 17 of 32 widths (0 → 8-72, including the k=6 widths 36 and 42) and falls at 1. Target builds past 16 rows never use more VGPRs.
- The FFN launch keeps main's 16-row spill (256 VGPR, 2 spilled; 4 with the draft's dims). It serves only fallback layers.
- No pytest launches K2 at 9-16 rows. The hash check covers those widths, and c2 runs 14 rows.
- The ISA test uses FlyDSL privates and MiniMax-M3's `code_object` (as M3's ISA test does), and skips without `llvm-objdump` on PATH (the nightly ROCm image has it). It guards only the late base load.
- The DSv4-Pro copy (`deepseek_v4/amd/mono`, #61482) has its own `load_x8_rows` and `peer_bases`. It is not changed or checked here.

**Related.**
- **#63027** (TP2 tuned K1/K2) batches the same copies in its tuned builds (`load_x8_rows_all`, gated on `tuned`) and moves `stage_down`'s barrier into a new `down_sums`. Whichever lands second keeps one batched path, enabled by `tuned` or `push_bases`, and puts the base rebind before `down_sums`' barrier.
- **#64153** (draft) applies the same two fixes at TP8. It is stacked on this PR's previous head (92852abd06) and needs a rebase onto this version.
- **#63486** (draft) moves the test file. If it lands first, this PR's test follows it.
- **#61934** (closed, "No e2e gain observed") issued the FFN seam's static loads before their polls. Those are different loads from this PR's.

<details>
<summary>Sibling PRs (MI355X low-concurrency work)</summary>

None of these touches this PR's files: #63888, #63890, #63891 (#63885 is merged).

#63893 (tuned K1 at TP4, draft) is stacked on #63027. Its own commit also edits `run_ffn` and `build_mono_k2` (their scratch-layout lines, not this PR's) and moves the TP4 K2's scratch offsets.
</details>

<details>
<summary>Compile-level evidence (gfx950, FlyDSL 0.4.0, COMPILE_ONLY=1, main f97a8d6647)</summary>

553 builds per tree: 505 gfx950 and 48 gfx942 (the three 48-row gfx942 K2 builds fail on both trees). The TP4 K2 is built at every width from 1 to 48 (314 builds). With this PR none of the 314 uses scratch; on main 21 do.

| TP4 K2 build | main | this PR |
|---|---|---|
| 14 rows, ratio 0 / 1 / 2 | 255 VGPR, 4 spilled, 20 B scratch, 4 reload waits between peer stores, 23 copy chains | 248 VGPR, no spill, no scratch, 3 chains |
| 14 rows, index source | 255 VGPR, 4 spilled, 20 B, 4 reload waits | 248 VGPR, no spill |
| 15 / 16 rows | 256 / 255-256 VGPR, 2 / 4 spilled | 242 VGPR, no spill |
| 13 rows, index source | 256 VGPR, 2 spilled, 12 B | 248 VGPR, no spill |
| 1-13 rows (1-12 at index sources) | 246-252 VGPR, 25 or 23 chains | 230-248 VGPR, 3 or 4 chains |
| DSpark draft K2, 1-16 rows (ratio 0, as the runner builds it) | 166-207 VGPR, 23-25 chains | 161-181 VGPR, 3-4 chains |
| 17-48 rows, every width, ratios 0/1/2 and index sources | 231-234 VGPR, 22-23 chains | 231-233 VGPR, 22-23 chains (only the base loads move) |
| DSpark draft K2, 17-48 rows | 171-234 VGPR | 171-233 VGPR |
| TP2 K1/K2, TP8 K1/K2, every TP4 K1, the FFN launch at TP2/TP4/TP8, gfx942 TP2/TP4 | | binary-identical (236 configs hashed: 191 gfx950, 45 gfx942) |

Copy chain = `buffer_load_dwordx4` → `s_waitcnt vmcnt(0)` → `ds_write_b128`. Reload wait = a `vmcnt(0)` between two system-scope peer stores.
</details>

## Overview

Removes the Huawei Ascend content from the 9 vLLM recipes that carry it. [vllm-project/vllm-ascend](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm-ascend/tree/main/recipes/overlays) already ships the same content as overlays, and vllm-project/recipes merges them at build time (vllm-project/recipes#1160), so the site keeps rendering it.

## Claims

- Ascend hardware keys, variants, overrides and hardware notes now have a single owner, vllm-ascend. Commands rendered on recipes.vllm.ai do not change.
- The one visible change is pill order on Kimi-K3: the `ascend_w4a8` variant moves after `fp8`, because overlay variants render last.
- vllm-project/recipes can enable `scope.exclude_brands: [Huawei]` on the `vllm` source once this merges and the lock bumps, which stops Ascend content from returning here.

## Validation

Compared the renderer's full JSON API output (`be6e6b2`) for vLLM `16d667348d` plus vllm-ascend `6d2866b717`, before and after this change:

```bash
# Same check as this repo's Recipes PR check
node scripts/validate-source.mjs --source vllm --dir <this branch>/recipes
# ✓ vllm recipes ... are valid against the renderer
```

- Current `main` with `exclude_brands: [Huawei]`: strict assemble fails on these 9 recipes.
- This branch with `exclude_brands: [Huawei]`: strict assemble and the JSON API build both pass.
- Output diff, ignoring provenance (`source`): 22,589 files before and after, none added or removed. 22,558 are identical, and the rest differ only in order. `models.json` swaps two Kimi-K3 entries, and about 30 recipe JSON files change key order (for example `meta.hardware`). The Kimi-K3 variant move above is the only order change that affects the page; variant and strategy order is unchanged on the other affected recipes.
- The Qwen3.8-27B guide renders byte-identical (SHA-1 checked), with the Ascend section placed at its `<!-- overlay:vllm-ascend:ascend -->` marker.
- `pre-commit run --files <changed files>` passes.

This changes recipe metadata only, so no model evaluation applies. Nothing was run on Ascend hardware, since the rendered commands are unchanged.

## Details

**Merge order:** this PR → lock bump in vllm-project/recipes → `exclude_brands: [Huawei]` there. Enabling the scope first would fail this repo's Recipes check and every lock bump.

**What stays here:** the scope check covers hardware-keyed content only, so this PR leaves the following alone:
- Prose that mentions Ascend: `performance_headline`, descriptions, guide references, and the GLM-5.3-Flash guide. Cleaning these up is a separate decision.
- Ascend-only speculative modes such as `qwen3_5_mtp` ("MTP (Ascend)"). Overlays can't add a mode today, and these modes reference variants that now come from the overlay, so renaming such a variant in vllm-ascend needs a matching change here.

**Comments:** 91 comment lines recording Ascend evidence and rationale are removed, and the overlays don't carry them. They remain in this repo's git history and could be copied to vllm-ascend.

**Open PRs affected:** #62668 (Kimi-K3 Ascend) and #62794 (DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash Ascend A3) belong in vllm-ascend, where vllm-project/vllm-ascend#19991 and vllm-project/vllm-ascend#20065 are related. #65021, #64775 and #64070 touch the same files and may need a rebase.

**Not a duplicate:** searched open PRs for Ascend, overlay and recipe keywords. None of them removes this content.

commits.pr_title: [Bugfix][LoRA] Fix KeyError crash when a LoRA name is reloaded with requests in flight
commits.pr_body:
## Overview

Fixes #64570. This change compares both `lora_name` and `lora_int_id` in `LoRARequest`, so reloading an adapter under the same name while old requests are still running no longer kills the engine.

## Claims

- Fixes the `KeyError` in `convert_mapping` → `EngineDeadError` reported in #64570.
- In-flight requests keep using the old adapter, while new requests use the reloaded one.

## Validation

- Added a regression test that crashes with `EngineDeadError` on `main` and passes with this fix.
- Reproduced the unload/reload flow against a running server. On `main`, the engine exits; with this fix, both requests complete with their respective adapters and `/health` returns 200.
- MRV2: `LoraState.get_activate_loras` returns adapter IDs `[1]` on `main` and `[1, 2]` with this fix. Local CPU testing used MRV1; the GPU CI job covers MRV2.
- Related CPU suites: 58 passed (`tests/lora/test_worker.py::test_worker_apply_lora` fails the same way on `main` because it does not support CPU). `pre-commit` passed.
- No model eval: outputs change only for batches that crashed before.

<details>
<summary>Commands and output</summary>

Regression test:

```bash
VLLM_CPU_KVCACHE_SPACE=4 .venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/lora/test_lora_functions.py::test_same_lora_name_with_different_ids -v -s
```

`main`:

```
  File "vllm/lora/punica_wrapper/utils.py", line 101, in convert_mapping
    lora_id_to_index[x] if x > 0 else -1 for x in mapping.prompt_mapping
    ~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~^^^
KeyError: np.int64(2)
...
vllm.v1.engine.exceptions.EngineDeadError: EngineCore encountered an issue. See stack trace (above) for the root cause.
============================== 1 failed in 30.67s ==============================
```

This PR:

```
tests/lora/test_lora_functions.py::test_same_lora_name_with_different_ids PASSED
============================== 1 passed in 27.57s ==============================
```

Server flow: `vllm serve Qwen/Qwen3-0.6B --enable-lora --max-loras 2 --max-lora-rank 8 --max-model-len 1024 --enforce-eager` with `VLLM_ALLOW_RUNTIME_LORA_UPDATING=True`. Load `pet` (meow adapter), start a 200-token stream on `pet`, unload `pet`, load `pet` again (woof adapter), load one more adapter so the new `pet` ID is evicted from its slot, then request `pet`.

- `main`: `KeyError: np.int64(2)` → `EngineDeadError`; both requests fail and the server exits.
- This PR: the old stream returns `Meow Meow Meow Meow Meow…`, the new request returns `Woof Woof Woof Woof Woof`, and `/health` returns 200.

</details>

## Details

`LoRARequest` currently compares only adapter names. If an adapter is unloaded and reloaded under the same name while old requests are still running, the worker can treat the old and new IDs as one adapter. The missing ID then causes `convert_mapping` to raise `KeyError`, killing the engine.

This does not change when unload takes effect or whether it waits for in-flight requests.

Not a duplicate: no open PR references #64570 or changes `LoRARequest` equality. I searched open PRs by the issue number and by `convert_mapping`, `LoRARequest`, `unload_lora_adapter` and `make_lora_inputs`.

commits.pr_title: [Bugfix][Frontend] Fix tool_reference results on DeepSeek V4.1 and /v1/messages
commits.pr_body:
<!-- markdownlint-disable -->

## Overview

The DeepSeek V4.1 encoder rejects `tool_reference` content parts with a 400, and `/v1/messages` turns a `tool_result` with `tool_reference` items into two `tool` messages for one call. This renders each reference on V4.1 as the tool's name and emits one `tool` message per `tool_result`, so conversations that use Claude Code's tool search work on DeepSeek V4.1 and render one result per tool call.

## Claims

- Requests with `tool_reference` parts render on DeepSeek V4.1. On main they fail with `DeepSeek V4.1 supports text and image content only; got 'tool_reference'`. This covers `tool_result` blocks with `tool_reference` items on `/v1/messages`, and `tool_reference` parts on `/v1/chat/completions`.
- On V4.1, each reference renders as the tool's name inside its call's `<tool_result>`. Several references are joined with `\n\n`, the separator the encoder already uses between parts.
- `/v1/messages` emits one `tool` message per `tool_result`: the `tool_reference` parts first, then the text. On main, a tool search result renders an extra empty result before the references, on GLM-5.3 as well as V4.1, so after parallel tool calls the results no longer line up with the calls.
- Templates that expand references keep working: GLM-5.3 renders the referenced tool definitions as before.
- A `tool_result` without `tool_reference` items converts as before, and other unsupported part types still return 400 on V4.1.
- The change is in `_convert_user_tool_result` (`vllm/entrypoints/anthropic/serving.py`) and `_normalize_messages` (`vllm/tokenizers/deepseek_v41.py`): 15 lines added and 11 removed, plus three tests.

## Validation

| Check | Command | main `5d55ef1590` | This PR |
|---|---|---|---|
| New tests | `pytest tests/entrypoints/anthropic/test_anthropic_messages_conversion.py::TestToolResultContent::test_tool_result_with_tool_references tests/entrypoints/scale_out/render/test_render.py::test_messages_render_tool_search_result_for_deepseek_v41 tests/tokenizers_/test_deepseek_v41.py::test_tool_references_render_as_tool_names` | 3 failed (below) | 3 passed |
| Changed test files | `pytest tests/entrypoints/anthropic/test_anthropic_messages_conversion.py tests/entrypoints/scale_out/render/test_render.py tests/tokenizers_/test_deepseek_v41.py tests/tokenizers_/test_deepseek_v4.py` | 271 passed, 4 failed (the 3 new tests and 1 below) | 274 passed, 1 failed (below) |
| `vllm launch render` with the DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash config and tokenizer, 4 requests (below) | | 4 of 4 HTTP 400 | 4 of 4 HTTP 200, one `<tool_result>` per call |
| `vllm launch render` with the GLM-5.3 config, tokenizer and chat template, 3 requests (below) | | 3 of 3 HTTP 200, one extra `<tool_response>` each | 3 of 3 HTTP 200, one `<tool_response>` per call |

The conversion test sends a `tool_result` with text, two `tool_reference` items and an image, and checks for one `tool` message with the references first, followed by the image's `user` message. The render test starts `vllm launch render deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash` through `RemoteLaunchRenderServer`, which downloads only the config and tokenizer, like the existing GPT-OSS render test. It sends a `/v1/messages` turn where a tool search and a file read ran in parallel, and checks the rendered user turn through `/detokenize`. On main the new tests fail like this:

```
E       AssertionError: assert ['assistant',...user', 'tool'] == ['assistant', 'tool', 'user']
E           AssertionError: {"error":{"message":"DeepSeek V4.1 supports text and image content only; got 'tool_reference'","type":"BadRequestError","param":null,"code":400}}
E                       ValueError: DeepSeek V4.1 supports text and image content only; got 'tool_reference'
3 failed, 3 warnings in 18.48s
```

With only the V4.1 encoder change and main's converter, the render test still fails: the parallel turn renders three `<tool_result>`s for two calls.

The one other failure in the changed files is `test_tokenize_matches_chat_render_for_gpt_oss`, which fails the same way on main here because the container cannot download the Harmony vocab file. Tests ran on CPU in `vllm-ci-postmerge-repo:074c83a09a0b872cec92e244d91adf2b3c55e41b-arm64-cpu` with the branch tree on `PYTHONPATH`. The repo's pre-commit hooks pass, including `ruff`, `mypy` and the test tethering check. No model evaluation is included: the change only affects prompts with `tool_reference` items.

<details>
<summary>Render server checks</summary>

**DeepSeek V4.1.** The server runs `vllm launch render deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash --tokenizer-mode deepseek_v41 --reasoning-parser deepseek_v41 --tool-call-parser deepseek_v41 --enable-auto-tool-choice --language-model-only`, with `config.json` and the tokenizer from revision `314113f8` and no weights. Every request declares a `ToolSearch` tool, plus `get_weather` and `get_time` with `defer_loading: true`.

1. `/v1/messages/render`, shaped like a Claude Code tool search: the last user turn is a `tool_result` whose content is `[{"type": "tool_reference", "tool_name": "get_weather"}]`.
2. The same conversation one turn later, after `get_weather` was called and returned.
3. `/v1/chat/completions/render` with a `tool` message whose content is `[{"type": "tool_reference", "name": "get_weather"}]`.
4. `/v1/messages/render` where one assistant turn calls `ToolSearch` and `Read` in parallel, and the user turn returns the reference result and a text result.

On main all four return the 400 above. On this branch, requests 1 and 3 end with `<tool_result>get_weather</tool_result>` before the generation prompt, request 2 has one result for each of its two calls, request 4 ends with `<tool_result>get_weather</tool_result>\n\n<tool_result>NOTES-FILE-BODY</tool_result>`, and the system prompt of every request lists all tools.

**GLM-5.3.** The server runs `vllm launch render` with the GLM-5.3 `config.json` and tokenizer, the chat template from Hub revision `ba32f8c19c`, `--tool-call-parser glm47 --reasoning-parser glm45 --enable-auto-tool-choice`, and requests 1 and 4 above plus a third `/v1/messages` request whose `tool_result` holds a text block and a `tool_reference`.

| Request | main | This PR |
|---|---|---|
| Tool search | `<tool_response></tool_response><tool_response><tools>{get_weather}</tools></tool_response>` | `<tool_response><tools>{get_weather}</tools></tool_response>` |
| Parallel `ToolSearch` + `Read` | 3 `<tool_response>`s for 2 calls, the first one empty | `<tool_response><tools>{get_weather}</tools></tool_response><tool_response>NOTES-FILE-BODY</tool_response>` |
| Text and reference in one result | `<tool_response>Found 1 tool</tool_response><tool_response><tools>{get_weather}</tools></tool_response>` | `<tool_response><tools>{get_weather}</tools></tool_response>` |

`{get_weather}` stands for the tool's full JSON definition, which both arms render identically.

</details>

## Details

**Root cause.** #40190 added `tool_reference` parts. `_convert_user_tool_result` emits a `tool` message with the result's text (empty for a plain tool search), then a second `tool` message with the `tool_reference` items, both for the same `tool_use_id`. An image in the result goes into a `user` message between the two. Templates and encoders that render one result per `tool` message render one result too many. Separately, V4.1 renders with its own encoder, and `_normalize_messages` raises `ValueError` for any part type other than text and image. The `tool_result` stays in the conversation history, so on V4.1 every later request in that conversation fails too, and an agent session that runs a tool search cannot continue.

**Why one message, references first.** Templates that expand references look for a `tool` message whose first part is a `tool_reference` (GLM-5.3's does), so the references lead and the text follows. Images stay in the `user` message after the `tool` message. Limitation: GLM-5.3's template expands such a message and skips its other parts, so text that sits beside references in one `tool_result` no longer renders there; on main it rendered as an extra result. The tool search docs show results that hold only `tool_reference` blocks.

**Why the name.** `apply_chat_template` puts every request tool into the V4.1 system prompt, deferred ones included, so the definitions a reference points at are already in context.
