commits.pr_body:
## Overview

With the V2 model runner and speculative decoding, a request that sets `logprob_token_ids` (and no `logprobs`) gets no logprobs back whenever another request in the same batch has draft tokens. `RejectionSampler` only looked at `max_num_logprobs`, so `logprob_token_ids` was dropped on that path. The regular V2 `Sampler` already handles it through `get_logprobs_dims`.

`/v1/systemone` reads are such requests (`max_tokens=1`, `logprob_token_ids`): next to a streaming chat on an MTP model, every read failed with `HTTP 400: No logprobs available for item 0`. This passes the per-request token ids to `compute_topk_scores` in the rejection sampler. Related: #42592 / #44727 (the same kind of mixed batch, on the V1 sampler, a different file).

## Claims

- Qwen3.8-27B with MTP 3, 6 `/v1/systemone` calls (4 questions, 2k-token state) while 4 chat streams run: 6/6 fail before, 6/6 succeed after.
- Chat is not affected: time to first token 0.52 → 0.60 s and inter-chunk latency p50 191 → 192 ms with and without systemone on the engine.
- The returned probabilities are not changed by the chat load: mean absolute difference 0.007 (max 0.041) between a cold call and the same call next to chat, the same as between a cold call and the same call repeated alone on a cached state (0.007, max 0.039).
- Batches without `logprob_token_ids` are unchanged (`compute_topk_scores` takes its fast path when `max_token_ids == 0`); without speculative decoding this code path is not used.

## Validation

Qwen3.8-27B 4-bit with MTP 3 on gfx1151 (Radeon 8060S), nightly `0.31.1rc1.dev273` (`2eb491e18b`), V2 model runner, `--enable-prefix-caching --mamba-cache-mode align --logprobs-mode raw_logprobs`, `--max-num-seqs 8`. The same change was applied to the nightly's copy of the file for the runs. Chat: 4 closed-loop streaming requests (256 tokens).

| | systemone alone | systemone + 4 chats, main | systemone + 4 chats, this PR |
|---|---|---|---|
| errors | 0 / 6 | 6 / 6 (HTTP 400, no logprobs) | 0 / 6 |
| chat errors | | 0 | 0 |

After the review changes the run was repeated (mixed: 0 errors, cold vs next-to-chat mean absolute difference 0.004, max 0.033). The same server also runs `/v1/systemone` accuracy (120 synthetic tickets: 0.90 / 0.67 / 1.00, unchanged) and the question-count cases (6.4 / 8.2 / 11.9 / 28.7 s for 1 / 4 / 16 / 64 questions, unchanged) with the change applied. MTP off, on main: no errors (no drafts, so the batch does not go through the rejection sampler); not re-run with the change.

Tests:

```bash
pytest tests/v1/worker/test_gpu_rejection_sampler_chunking.py tests/v1/worker/test_gpu_batch_shard.py
```

31 passed with the change. New tests in `test_gpu_rejection_sampler_chunking.py` build a real `LogprobTokenIdsState` and check the returned ids and scores against `log_softmax` / the raw logits for every row:
- `test_logprob_token_ids_without_topk_logprobs`: token ids only, raw and logits modes, and nothing is computed when none are requested;
- `test_logprob_token_ids_with_topk_logprobs`: top-k `logprobs=1` narrower than the widest `logprob_token_ids`, requests with and without ids;
- `test_logprob_token_ids_with_adaptive_verification`: one chunk over compacted logits, device `cu_num_logits` and a host-side upper bound, same result as the fixed-boundary layout;
- `test_get_logprobs_dims_with_only_token_ids`.

`test_gather_sampler_output_logprobs_and_nans` is parametrized over top-k only, token ids only and token ids wider than top-k. The CUDA tests of these files are skipped on ROCm by `current_platform.is_cuda()`; I ran them locally with that check replaced by `torch.cuda.is_available()`. The new tests fail on main. The `model_runner.py` call site of the sharded gather (TP > 1) has no test and was not run.

## Details

- `RejectionSampler.__call__` calls `Sampler.get_logprobs_dims` once and passes `logprobs_dims` to `_verify_in_chunks` and `_get_logprobs_tensors`, which also takes the chunk's `expanded_idx_mapping` (`compute_topk_scores` needs it to map each logits row to its request).

- Not covered: DSpark and the other speculators were not run; they go through the same `RejectionSampler.__call__`.

commits.pr_title: [Bugfix][ROCm] Fix Kimi K3 online quantization with padded projections
commits.pr_body:
## Overview

Fix ROCm Kimi K3 online weight loading so its padded merged KDA projection finishes as soon as all checkpoint shards arrive. Following review, the fix lives in an AMD-local `_PaddedKimiGDNMergedColumnParallelLinear`, mirroring the NVIDIA implementation; no shared loader code is changed.

### Summary

```text
six KDA checkpoint shards arrive
  → complete using real elements, excluding alignment rows (weight_loader_numel)
  → layerwise processing materializes the weight and replays the loads
  → loader re-zeroes the padding rows
  → process the layer and release its input tensors
```

## Claims

- Avoid accumulating full GPU checkpoint tensors across incomplete KDA layers during online quantization.
- Keep the alignment padding zero after online materialization, which allocates with `empty_strided` and drops the constructor's zero-init.
- Only `vllm/models/kimi_k3/amd/kda.py` changes; the shared Kimi-Linear projection and `reload/meta.py` are untouched.

## Validation

### Evidence

Local regression on ROCm (`vllm/vllm-openai-rocm:nightly` container), using the KDA online-loading test from this PR's first revision as an out-of-tree harness: real `KimiK3DeltaAttention` construction at TP8, two TP ranks × two shard orders × padded/unpadded head counts, `empty_strided` poisoned with NaN.

| Configuration | Result |
| --- | --- |
| `main` | 4 padded cases fail: projection stays on meta and holds all six sources |
| This PR | 8 pass |
| This PR with loader re-zeroing disabled | 4 padded cases fail: padding rows are NaN |

```bash
pytest tests/models/kimi_k3/test_amd_kda_fused_conv1d.py \
  tests/models/kimi_k3/test_amd_kda_direct_return.py \
  tests/models/kimi_k3/test_amd_kda_checkpoint.py \
  tests/models/kimi_k3/test_kda.py tests/models/kimi_k3/test_kda_metadata.py \
  tests/models/test_alice_ai.py -q
# 181 passed, 31 skipped (MI355X)
pytest tests/models/kimi_k3/test_amd_kda_decode.py -k test_decode_weights_staged_after_loading -q
# 4 passed
```

ruff passes; the mypy hook reports no new errors in `amd/kda.py` (28 vs. 29 pre-existing on `main`).

No unit test is added. The first revision's test imported the Kimi K3 KDA layer into the shared `model_executor` pytest process; that pulls in numba, which exposes a latent `triton_utils/dispatcher` issue and fails the Triton dispatcher tests that run afterwards. That dispatcher issue is independent of this fix and is left to a separate PR.

Full-model GPU validation used vLLM `81198e97ba7eee2a22540caaa756b7fdddcb4d93` plus the first revision of this fix (same `weight_loader_numel` accounting; padding zeroed during materialization instead of in the loader), on 2 × 8 MI355X GPUs, TP8/DCP8, fastsafetensors, target-model FP8 PTPC, DSpark4 with synthetic AL=3.36, C48/3600s. Both runs had the same P/D hosts and started with ~287.707 GiB free per GPU. The current revision has not been rerun at full-model scale.

| Measurement | [Original run](https://github.com/ROCm/ATOM/actions/runs/38805434237) | [Fixed run](https://github.com/ROCm/ATOM/actions/runs/38805460289) |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Loading | HSA out-of-resources at 10/12 checkpoint groups | All 16 workers loaded; 513 target online layers per worker |
| Maximum buffered GPU source references per worker | ~42.19 GiB | 0.451 GiB |
| Lowest sampled free VRAM, P / D | 22 / 88 MiB | 25.818 / 24.869 GiB |
| Benchmark | Did not start | Full 3600s coverage; 4224 successful requests |

Source-reference bytes overlap allocated/reserved memory and must not be added to those counters. This verifies loading and serving completion, not decoding accuracy or a throughput gain. The fixed run had 7 empty-content request errors and a 300s cancel-drain timeout, retained in the run logs.

## Details

At TP8, KDA's local merged projection has 6284 real rows and 4 alignment rows. Without `weight_loader_numel`, online processing waits for 6288 rows although the checkpoint only provides the six real projections, so it defers processing and retains every source until model finalization. With GPU-backed fastsafetensors inputs this exhausts VRAM before loading completes.

During online loading the constructor's padding `zero_()` runs on meta, and materialization allocates with `empty_strided`. Layerwise processing then replays the buffered calls through the layer's weight loader, so re-zeroing the padding rows there restores them. `CopyCounter` only counts `copy_`, so the zeroing does not affect completion accounting. It adds no steady-state inference work.

The subclass extends the shared Kimi-Linear projection instead of importing the NVIDIA class, which would pull NVIDIA backend modules into the ROCm path and change AMD loading through its block-scale replication.

**Related work / duplicate check:** #50523 fixes general zero initialization for rematerialized weights; it does not declare KDA's loadable size and does not resolve this source-retention failure. If it lands, the loader re-zeroing becomes redundant but harmless. Open KDA quantization PRs and #61287 were also checked; no matching KDA completion fix was found.

### Merge Danger

**Door:** two-way. **Blast Radius:** Kimi K3 ROCm KDA weight loading.

AI assistance was used: Codex prepared the first revision; Claude Code prepared the review revision and the CI analysis. Results above describe agent-run validation.

commits.pr_title: [Bugfix][Mooncake] Let decodes reuse divergent local hybrid prefix hits
commits.pr_body:
## Overview

`MooncakeConnector` does not opt into `supports_divergent_local_hybrid_hits` (#50344), so a hybrid-model decode (attention plus Mamba, GDN or KDA) drops its local attention hit and pulls the whole prompt from P every turn. This opts the `kv_consumer` role in, as MoRIIO READ and NIXL already do.

## Claims

- On a hybrid model, a Mooncake decode keeps its local attention prefix and pulls only the uncached suffix plus the recurrent state.
- `kv_producer` and `kv_both` keep the current lookup.

## Validation

- Kimi-K3 1P1D on MI355X, Mooncake RDMA, multi-turn agentic replay at concurrency 48: decode local prefix hit rate 0.0% to 93.9%; draft acceptance 58.78% to 58.79% (MoRIIO READ 58.79%).
- The new scheduler test fails on main and passes here. Mooncake unit tests: 164 passed. pre-commit clean.

<details><summary>Request flow, test output and serving numbers</summary>

Turn k of a session whose prompt extends turn k-1:

1. The router sends the request to P with `do_remote_decode`; P prefills and pushes KV.
2. On D, the attention blocks pulled in turn k-1 are still cached. Mamba has no state at any block boundary, since D never computes those positions.
3. Before: `get_computed_blocks` returns the hit every group shares, 0 tokens. Mooncake asks for N-1 tokens and pulls every attention block plus the state slot.
4. After: `get_computed_blocks_for_connector` returns the attention hit H. Mooncake asks for N-1-H tokens and pulls the suffix blocks plus the state slot; P pairs the last blocks of each group.
5. D decodes from the recurrent state P computed at N-1.

Unit test, on main and on this branch:

```
$ pytest -q tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_mooncake_connector_hybrid_mamba.py -k keeps_local_attention_prefix
# main
E       assert 6 == 2
E        +  where 6 = len([9, 10, 11, 12, 13, 14])
FAILED ...::test_hybrid_gdn_remote_prefill_keeps_local_attention_prefix[kv_consumer-2]
1 failed, 1 passed, 11 deselected
# this branch
2 passed, 11 deselected

$ pytest -q tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_mooncake_connector_hybrid_mamba.py \
    tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_mooncake_connector_hma.py \
    tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_mooncake_connector.py
164 passed
```

Serving, Kimi-K3 1P1D, decode flags `--tensor-parallel-size 8 --block-size 128 --kv-cache-dtype fp8 --kv-transfer-config '{"kv_connector":"MooncakeConnector","kv_role":"kv_consumer","kv_connector_extra_config":{"mooncake_protocol":"rdma"}}'`, aiperf multi-turn agentic trace replay at concurrency 48. One run per column.

| Decode metric | Mooncake before | Mooncake after | MoRIIO READ |
|---|---|---|---|
| Local prefix cache hit rate (log) | 0.0% | 93.9% | 91.2% |
| Prompt tokens, `local_cache_hit` / `external_kv_transfer` | 0 / 801.7M | not recorded | 731.3M / 70.9M |
| Draft acceptance | 58.78% | 58.79% | 58.79% |
| TTFT mean / p50, same request window | 2984 / 1727 ms | 3137 / 1730 ms | 2611 / 1365 ms |

The "after" run was cancelled by the cluster after 4598 requests, so it has no end-of-run Prometheus snapshot; its hit rate is the decode's periodic log line. MoRIIO's hit rate is `local_cache_hit` over all prompt tokens.

</details>

## Details

A decode never computes the block boundaries of a pulled prompt, so it caches attention blocks but no recurrent state. With the opt-in, the scheduler keeps the attention hit, and `update_state_after_alloc` already pulls every transfer group's unhashed blocks, the state slot included. With nothing to pull, the scheduler falls back to the reconciled lookup (#50344).

Only `kv_consumer` opts in: the per-group lookup reports a shared-prefix boundary of 0, which would disable junction checkpoints on roles that prefill locally.

Limitations:
- Serving runs used vLLM 81198e97 with this property forced to True on the decode, matching this PR; not re-run on main.
- Under `MultiConnector` every child must opt in until #63041.
- TTFT did not change on this workload.

Not a duplicate: the open Mooncake PRs (#53730, #63420, #63425) do not touch this property. AI assistance (Claude in Cursor) was used to write the change, the test and this description.

commits.pr_title: [Perf][FlashAttention] FA4: pass no FP8 descale for a unit per-tensor scale
commits.pr_body:
<!-- markdownlint-disable -->

## Overview

For an FP8 KV cache whose per-tensor scales are 1.0, FlashAttention now passes FA4 no descale at all. Before, it passed broadcast descale views that FA4 copied into contiguous tensors, three copy kernels per attention layer and step.

This PR began as the squash of the whole MiniMax-M3.1-Flash tree. That squash has since been split into the PRs below; this PR now holds only the FA4 change.

## How #63232 was split

| Part of the original squash | Where it went | State |
|---|---|---|
| MiniMax-M3.1 model and DSpark draft model, with their kernels (MSA NVFP4 KV cache and indexer, MegaMoE staging, ROCm MXFP8 linears, ...) | #64111 | merged |
| ROCm: NVFP4 MoE re-quantization to MXFP4/MXFP8, and fused shared experts through online quantization | #64378 | merged |
| FA4: no FP8 descale for a unit per-tensor scale | this PR | open |
| NIXL P/D: re-sharding NVFP4 KV pages across heterogeneous TP (`AttentionSpec.kv_head_major_slots`) | #64475 | open |
| Scheduler: keep KV cache zeroing for mixed-precision `UniformTypeKVCacheSpecs` groups | #64472 | open |
| DSpark/DFlash draft step: Markov bias in the Gumbel kernel, wider DFlash padding, `is_padding` from the positions kernel, top-p fix | #64476 | open |
| Batch-sharded DSpark draft sampling | dropped from #64476; #63886 covers it | open (#63886) |
| SimpleCPUOffload: one host buffer per rank with HugeTLB pages | already open as #60130; the squash's extra ROCm change (SDMA copy-engine flag for batched copies) was pushed onto #60130 | open (#60130) |
| Scheduler draft-slot change | dropped: `main`'s `max_num_new_slots_for_drafting` already returns 0 for DFlash/DSpark | – |
| Sparse paged-attention KV block count fix (ROCm) | dropped: already on `main` via #63270 | – |

The full squash as it was before the split is a0ea941097 (on 5d35ce3934), in this PR's force-push history.

PRs that were opened against this branch (`minimax-m31-flash`) while it held the squash: #64359, #64273, #64264, #64206, #63528, #63491 and #62509. Their diffs against this branch now include the whole old squash (e.g. #64359 shows 193 files). The model (#64111) and the ROCm re-quantization (#64378) are on `main`, so they can retarget `main`.

## Claims

- **Unit scales:** when FA4 runs with a per-tensor Q/K/V scale of exactly 1.0, `FlashAttentionImpl` passes `None` for that descale.
  - FA4 reads a missing descale as 1.0, so the output is bit-identical.
  - FA4's `maybe_contiguous` no longer copies the three broadcast descale views per layer and step.
- **Other scales:** calibrated per-tensor scales and per-head scales keep their descale tensors. Other FlashAttention versions get the same broadcast descale as before; only the strides of its size-1 dims are made canonical, which changes metadata, not values.
- **(1, 1) descale views:** a view with one sequence and one KV head per rank now gets canonical strides. FA4 treats such a view as contiguous and skips its copy, and its layout check then rejects the zero stride.

## Validation

On GB300:

```bash
pytest tests/v1/attention/test_attention_backends.py
```

148 passed, 9 skipped, 4 failed. The 4 failures are `test_sliding_window_encoder_backend_correctness` (embeddinggemma-300m). They fail the same way on `main` (2abde627d9) in this environment.

The new `test_flash_attn_fa4_unit_fp8_descale_is_exact` (Blackwell only) checks that:

- a unit scale gives no descale;
- FA4's output with no descale equals its output with the broadcast unit descale, bit for bit;
- a descale of 2 changes the output, so the comparison is not vacuous;
- calibrated and per-head scales keep their descale tensors.

Not covered:

- No end-to-end benchmark on this branch; the three copy kernels saved per layer and step were not timed.
- No accuracy eval: the output is bit-identical by the test above.
- The (1, 1) stride case is not in the new test, which uses 3 sequences and 4 KV heads.

## Details

- **Why the check is on the host:** the scales are fixed once the weights are loaded, so the `_scale_float` mirrors decide the case on the host with no GPU sync. A per-head scale's float mirror holds only its maximum, so the check also requires a single-element scale.
- **Compiled kernels:** FA4 compiles a separate kernel without descales, since descale presence is part of its compile key. A model with unit scales always takes that kernel.
- **Not a duplicate:** the open FA4 PRs change other things. #48156 warms up the paged FA4 kernels, #60372 adds SM90 FP8 MMA for Gemma-4, #63328 is sparse-MLA FP8 prefill, and #54705 covers Inkling per-tensor scales outside `flash_attn.py`. None of them changes how `FlashAttentionImpl` passes descales.

Credits: qizixi wrote the FA4 change and is a co-author in the commit. AI assistance (Claude) was used to split the original squash into the PRs above, to write the FA4 test and to draft this description. The submitter reviewed the change and ran the tests above.

encoders of the Nemotron-3.5-Transcribe audio tower, the ASR encoder and the Sortformer speaker encoder, now run only
each row's valid frames, packed row after row, and attend through `MMEncoderAttention` with `cu_seqlens` instead of
padded, masked SDPA. The PR changes the model file, its tests and its docs note only.

## Claims

- The tower attends through vLLM's multimodal encoder attention: vLLM selects the platform's variable-length kernel
  (FlashAttention on the tested GPUs), and `--mm-encoder-attn-backend` applies to the tower.
- The tower is faster on batches of many clips (BF16, tower only): 3.1× and 2.5× on 32 and 64 clips on an RTX PRO
  6000, 1.51× and 2.15× on H100. On H100 it is slower on 8 clips and on 4 long clips (0.85× and 0.84×). Offline
  end-to-end RTFx on the RTX PRO 6000 quick sets does not change.
- Quick-set WER changes are small. On the long sets, AMI-IHM cpWER rises by 1.73 points, all from one meeting whose
  speaker attribution the packed tower changes in every run (six runs per arm, with GPUs swapped and request order
  shuffled); Earnings22 WER rises by 0.32 points from a few looping recordings whose link to the tower change is not
  known.
- `mm_encoder_attn_dtype='fp8'` is refused with a clear error. The FP8 and NVFP4 checkpoints quantize the linear
  layers of the tower's ASR encoder without this setting and are not affected.

## Validation

Setups:

- Desktop: one RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell (FlashAttention 2) and the BF16 checkpoint
  `nvidia/NVIDIA-Nemotron-3.5-Transcribe-30B-A4B` at the released revision `525be0e`; the quick sets ran earlier with
  the pre-release revision `f6e8392` of the same repository. The exactness and accuracy check, the batch-dependence
  probe and the tower timing ran this branch; the quick and long sets ran the same model-file changes on pre-merge
  builds of #64282 (the long-set build, in both arms, also carries follow-up commits outside the tower).
- H100: one H100 80GB HBM3 (FlashAttention 3), vLLM `0.32.1rc1.dev326+gc722f3a53` with this PR's tower code (the same
  executable code; only the license header differs) and torch 2.14.0+cu130. The exactness and accuracy check used
  weights byte-identical to the released checkpoint; the tower timing and batch-dependence probes used the
  pre-release GA-RC1 BF16 weights (SHA-256 `fe3b898b42a65837180c65dedd2e62b92836cee704ae3cbee2f473946fc7d0c9`).

**Tests** (this branch on main `e0d00e4b8e`; Python 3.12.14, torch 2.14.0+cu132, pytest 9.1.1):

```bash
pytest tests/models/multimodal/processing/test_nemotron3_5_transcribe.py    # RTX PRO 6000: 30 passed
CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES= VLLM_TARGET_DEVICE=cpu \
  pytest tests/models/multimodal/processing/test_nemotron3_5_transcribe.py  # 30 passed
pre-commit run --files docs/models/supported_models.md \
  tests/models/multimodal/processing/test_nemotron3_5_transcribe.py \
  vllm/model_executor/models/nemotron3_5_transcribe_audio.py                # passed (ruff 0.14.0, mypy, typos, markdownlint)
```

The new tests fail without their code: the empty-batch test with the guard removed (vLLM's SDPA wrapper raises
`torch.cat(): expected a non-empty list of Tensors`), and the FP8 test with the refusal removed (vLLM's generic FP8
check raises a different message). The tiny tower is float32 and selects TORCH_SDPA, so the tests do not cover
FlashAttention; the real-tower measurements below do. CI runs the file in the CPU Multimodal Processor step.

**Exactness and accuracy** (each clip encoded alone; 64 short and 4 long clips; the released checkpoint). With
float32 and vLLM's TORCH_SDPA backend, the packed tower is bit-identical to main's padded tower for 68 of 68 clips at
the ASR states, speaker probabilities and embeddings, on both the RTX PRO 6000 and H100. In BF16, against that
float32 reference, both towers have the same typical error (ASR relative L2 median about 7e-3 on short clips on both
GPUs). On the four long clips, FlashAttention 2 (RTX PRO 6000) matches main's error (788 against 843 flipped speaker
frames of 4,314), while FlashAttention 3 (H100) has somewhat larger worst-case errors (ASR maximum 0.043 against
0.036; 358 against 316 flipped frames).

**Tower speed** (BF16, tower only, median of 10 alternating runs):

| Batch | Padded, RTX PRO 6000 (ms) | Packed, RTX PRO 6000 (ms) | Packed speedup, H100 |
|---|---|---|---|
| 8 clips | 15.7 | 13.8 | 0.85× |
| 32 clips | 107.2 | 34.1 | 1.51× |
| 64 clips | 148.7 | 60.0 | 2.15× |
| 4 clips of 55–115 s | 91.8 | 73.6 | 0.84× |

Offline end-to-end RTFx does not change (RTX PRO 6000, quick sets, English / multilingual: 386 / 428 packed, 390 /
426 padded): the tower does not limit serving throughput.

**Accuracy, quick sets** (offline; Open ASR leaderboard English, 18,341 rows scored as 18,006 entries; multilingual,
15,486 clips):

| Checkpoint | Padded WER (%) English / multilingual | Packed WER (%) English / multilingual |
|---|---|---|
| BF16 | 3.89 / 4.96 | 3.90 / 4.94 |

**Accuracy, long sets** (multi-speaker SOT, 164 sessions, cpWER; long-form, 451 recordings, WER with the loop
guardrail; padded and packed served side by side, each run twice):

| Set | Padded (%), run 1 / run 2 | Packed (%), run 1 / run 2 | Packed − padded (points) |
|---|---|---|---|
| SOT headline | 13.01 / 13.04 | 13.25 / 13.28 | +0.24 |
| SOT AMI-IHM | 10.27 / 10.50 | 12.04 / 12.20 | +1.73 |
| SOT AMI-SDM | 17.65 / 17.53 | 17.31 / 17.22 | −0.32 |
| SOT CHAES | 11.52 / 11.51 | 11.46 / 11.48 | −0.04 |
| SOT Mixer6 | 15.01 / 15.07 | 14.92 / 14.94 | −0.11 |
| Long-form CORAAL average | 14.78 / 13.59 | 13.61 / 14.84 | +0.04 |
| Long-form Earnings21 | 8.25 / 8.25 | 8.17 / 8.20 | −0.07 |
| Long-form Earnings22 | 12.36 / 12.55 | 12.81 / 12.74 | +0.32 |

CORAAL's mean moves by +0.04 points, against repeat differences of 1.19 (padded) and 1.23 (packed); Earnings21 moves
by −0.07. AMI-IHM's +1.73 comes from one of its 16 meetings (EN2002c): in both packed runs, about 800 words of one
speaker go to an extra speaker tag. The words are unchanged (WER without speaker tags moves by +0.07), so this is
speaker attribution, not recognition; an earlier H100 comparison with different weights moved the same meeting the
other way. Earnings22's +0.32 comes from nine recordings where generation loops or reaches the token limit, mostly as
deleted text; the other 116 recordings improve slightly. On H100 (one run per arm, an earlier checkpoint and chat
template), AMI-IHM and Earnings22 improved instead, while Mixer6 and three CORAAL locations got worse. A crossover on
SOT (four more runs per arm, with GPUs swapped and request order shuffled) reproduced the EN2002c split in all six
packed runs (about 915 words under the extra tag) and in none of the six padded runs (about 115 words), so it follows
the tower, not the GPU or the batch order. The other 15 AMI-IHM meetings are equal or slightly better with the packed
tower in every pair. Earnings22 was not part of the crossover. TED-LIUM (11 recordings) varies too much between runs
of the same code to compare (up to 5.9 points).

**Batch dependence (BF16).** A clip's tower output can depend on the other clips in its batch, before and after this
PR: rounding changes with the batch, the speaker encoder's probabilities move, and the thresholded speaker features
flip on some frames. Batched against alone:

| Tower | H100: identical clips, 64 short / 4 long | H100: flipped speaker frames, long clips (of 4,314) | RTX PRO 6000: flipped speaker frames, long clips (of 4,314) |
|---|---|---|---|
| Padded (SDPA) | 32 / 4 | 0 | 170 |
| Packed, FlashAttention | 32 / 2 | 44 | 216 |
| Packed, TORCH_SDPA forced | 32 / 4 | 0 | 316 |

On the four long clips on H100, forcing SDPA removed the additional speaker-feature variation of FlashAttention 3,
and the ASR encoder's output stayed identical with FlashAttention 3. Forcing SDPA does not make the tower
batch-invariant: on H100, half of the short clips change with the batch in all three towers (embeddings up to 0.033
relative L2 apart, no speaker flips), and on the RTX PRO 6000 all three towers flip speaker frames on three of the
four long clips. FlashAttention therefore stays the default. Forced SDPA on the RTX PRO 6000 takes 23.4, 63.8, 113.0
and 100.3 ms on the four batches of the speed table.

## Details

- **Packing.** `TransformerEncoder.pack` indexes each row's valid frames from host lengths and builds `cu_seqlens`
  with `MMEncoderAttention`'s helpers for the selected backend. Rotary embeddings use each frame's position in its
  row. Rows without valid frames are left out, and a batch without any valid frame skips the layers, because vLLM's
  SDPA wrapper cannot split an empty `cu_seqlens`. The padded positions of the output are zero. The Sortformer step
  adds its speaker-cache and FIFO context to the host lengths as to the device lengths.
- **Host lengths.** The tower already has the clip lengths on the host, so packing adds no device-to-host copy. With
  `TORCH_SDPA`, vLLM's SDPA wrapper still copies the cumulative lengths to the host once per layer
  (`vllm/v1/attention/ops/vit_attn_wrappers.py`).
- **FP8 encoder attention.** vLLM's encoder attention accepts `mm_encoder_attn_dtype='fp8'` only on the FlashInfer
  cuDNN backend and on ROCm AITER. There, the tower's attention layers would add FP8 scale buffers that no checkpoint
  has, so loading fails, and the FlashInfer path expects a different `cu_seqlens` layout. The tower therefore refuses
  the setting on every backend when it is built. The padded SDPA path ignored it.
- **Docs.** The model's note in `docs/models/supported_models.md` states the refusal and that the encoder attention
  backend and the other clips in a batch can change the tower's BF16 output.
- **Tradeoffs and limits.** On H100 the packed tower is slower than the padded one on 8 clips and on long clips, and
  serving throughput does not change. `MMEncoderAttention` has no per-layer backend option, so SDPA in the speaker
  encoder alone would need a model-specific override. Measured on RTX PRO 6000 and H100 only, not on ROCm or other
  GPUs.
- **Duplicate check.** No open PR mentions Nemotron-3.5-Transcribe (GitHub search, 2026-10-31).

commits.pr_title: [MRV2] Cap torch.topk rows in chunked prompt logprobs
commits.pr_body:
## Overview

Bound the `torch.topk` workspace in Model Runner V2's chunked prompt-logprobs computation by ranking each logits chunk in row blocks of at most 64M elements. Follow-up to #64841, whose preallocated outputs raised the peak for full-vocab prompt logprobs on short multi-chunk prompts.

## Claims

- Full-vocab prompt logprobs (152k vocab, fp16 logits) peak at **4.98 GiB** for a 2048-row prompt, down from 7.54 GiB before #64841 and 8.12 GiB with it; **11.94 GiB** at 8192 rows, down from 28.12 / 15.07 GiB.
- ~3.5% added latency, for full-vocab prompt logprobs only.
- No change for `k` below ~65k (e.g. the default `max_logprobs=20`): each chunk is still ranked in one `topk` call, with identical latency and peak.

## Validation

GB200, `compute_prompt_logprobs_with_chunking` on a 151936-vocab, 1536-hidden fp16 head, median of 20 runs (5 at full vocab); all variants return identical results:

| rows | k | before #64841 | #64841 (+ early frees) | this PR |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 2048 | 5 / 20 / 100 / 1000 | — | 3.50 / 3.51 / 3.52 / 3.59 ms | 3.50 / 3.50 / 3.52 / 3.57 ms |
| 2048 | 151936 | 7.54 GiB, 21.7 ms | 8.12 GiB, 21.45 ms | **4.98 GiB, 22.19 ms** |
| 8192 | 5 / 20 / 100 / 1000 | — | 13.76 / 13.77 / 13.81 / 14.06 ms | 13.75 / 13.78 / 13.81 / 14.07 ms |
| 8192 | 151936 | 28.12 GiB, 86.3 ms | 15.07 GiB, 85.56 ms | **11.94 GiB, 88.54 ms** |

Peak memory for k ≤ 1000 is 0.30–0.37 GiB in every variant.

```
pytest tests/v1/sample/test_logprobs.py -k "chunked_prompt_logprobs_match_unchunked or test_all_logprobs or prompt_logprobs_with_chunking_and_preemption or test_prompt_logprobs_mode or test_get_logprobs_and_prompt_logprobs"
16 passed, 7 skipped   # GB200, with a 32M cap; the unit test cases rerun with the final 64M cap: 4 passed
```

`test_chunked_prompt_logprobs_match_unchunked` gains a `split_topk` case that shrinks the cap so 100-row blocks straddle the chunk boundaries.

## Details

- `torch.topk` with k near the vocab size sorts each row; its workspace grows with rows × k, ~5.5 GiB for a 1024-row chunk of a 152k vocab, and was the step's peak. #64841 preallocates the whole prompt's outputs after the first chunk, so for a 2-chunk prompt they (plus the previous chunk's still-referenced results) sat on top of the second chunk's `topk`. The per-block results and per-chunk logits are now freed before the next block / chunk.
- Motivation: with measured KV cache sizing (#56492), the sizing warmup's largest prefill requests `max_logprobs` prompt logprobs, and `tests/entrypoints/openai/chat_completion/test_chat_echo.py` (`--max-logprobs 151936`) reserved ~7.5 GiB for this on an 18 GB H200 MIG slice, leaving no KV cache.
- Cap choice: 32M elements gives 3.80 GiB at 2048 rows but +20% latency; 128M would leave the 2048-row peak near 7.3 GiB.
- The Triton top-k/top-p sampler kernel isn't a substitute: it masks below a pivot rather than returning sorted ids, and logprob ranks are assigned by position, so full-vocab requests still need a full sort.

commits.pr_title: [Perf][DSv4.1] Vectorize first-layer HC expansion copy
commits.pr_body:
## Purpose

DeepSeek-V4.1's first decoder layer builds its `hc_mult` residual streams with `x.unsqueeze(1).expand(-1, hc_mult, -1).contiguous()`. This replaces it with `hc_expand`, a small Triton copy that reads each input element once and stores it to every stream. The output is the same contiguous `[M, hc_mult, H]` tensor, bit for bit.

The kernel lives in the DeepSeek-V4.1 mHC ops (`vllm/models/deepseek_v41/nvidia/ops/mhc.py`) and is called directly; DSv4.1 does not run under `torch.compile`, so no custom op is registered. Shared mHC kernels are unchanged.

## Results

GB300, DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash, TP1 / DP2 / EP2, DSpark K=5, FlashInfer autotune on. Full model-forward latency (target + DSpark), FI → HC → FI per shape, 3 samples × 5 iterations, 5 s warmup.

| Tokens / rank | Main | This PR | Reduction | Main drift |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| 8192 | 84.755 ms | 84.214 ms | 0.638% | +0.188% |
| 32768 | 292.447 ms | 291.563 ms | 0.302% | +0.276% |

- Hidden states and draft tokens are bitwise identical to main on both ranks.
- A single sequence; earlier prototype rounds gave 0.38% / 0.32% at 32K and no gain at 8K, so only the 32K gain is claimed.
- This revision moves the kernel into DeepSeek-V4.1 with the same indexing and launch. Re-checked against the measured commit (`be1a44dee6`) on 6 decode/prefill shapes, old → new → old in fresh processes: outputs bitwise identical, latency equal or up to 0.3% faster (within run-to-run drift).
- Copy alone at `[32768, 5120]`, `hc_mult=4`, BF16: 1321 → 241 µs (CUPTI, cold L2). PTX uses `ld.global.v4.b32` / `st.global.v4.b32`.

GSM8K (1319 questions, 5-shot, greedy, max 1024 tokens, same FI tactics):

| Concurrency | Main | This PR |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| 1 | 1192 (90.372%) | 1192 (90.372%), all responses and token counts identical |
| 32 | 1205 (91.357%) | 1198 (90.826%) |

C32 batches are dynamic and main itself is not output-stable there (two main runs flip 31 questions each way), so equal C32 accuracy is not claimed. 60 passkey cases at 8K/16K/32K match main's full responses and token counts.

## Test Plan

```bash
pytest tests/kernels/mhc/test_mhc_kernels.py -k hc_expand -v
```

GB300: 20 passed. `pre-commit` passes.

The test checks bitwise equality with `expand().contiguous()` in eager mode and under CUDA graph replay, for empty, strided and odd-sized inputs, NaN and −0.0. It runs in the existing B200 mHC CI job.

commits.pr_title: [Bugfix][DSv4.1] Autotune the sparse indexer's wq_b GEMM
commits.pr_body:
## Overview

Make FlashInfer autotune cover the DeepSeek-V4.1 sparse indexer's `wq_b` GEMM. In the autotune dummy run the indexer took its short-context path, which returns before `wq_b`, so that MXFP8 GEMM was never tuned. The autotune pass now tunes `wq_b` directly; the indexer forward is unchanged.

## Claims

- With `enable_flashinfer_autotune`, the indexer `wq_b` GEMM (K=1280, N=4096 on DSV4.1-Flash) is now tuned for every token bucket.
- Serving no longer hits untuned `mxfp8_gemm` shapes for it, so it no longer falls back to `CuteDSLMxfp8GemmRunner` and JIT-compiles mid-step.

## Validation

DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash, MRV2, MegaMoE + MegaAttention, DSpark K=5, `FULL_AND_PIECEWISE` graphs to 8190, `--max-num-batched-tokens 16384`, `--kernel-config '{"enable_flashinfer_autotune":true,"moe_backend":"deep_gemm_mega_moe"}'`. Both runs tuned from an empty `VLLM_FLASHINFER_AUTOTUNE_CACHE_DIR` with the same 22 token buckets (1 to 16384), so the entry counts are comparable.

| | main | this PR |
|---|---:|---:|
| `mxfp8_gemm` entries in the saved autotune cache (per rank) | 110 | 132 |
| ... of which `(1280, 4096)` (indexer `wq_b`) | 0 | 22 |
| `No tuned config covers mxfp8_gemm` warnings in the server log | 35 | 0 |
| ... after the server was ready (during serving) | 3 | 0 |

- main: GB300, DEP2 (TP1 × DP2 + EP2), prefill-only AgentX replay at concurrency 256.
- this PR: GB200, DEP4 (DEP2 does not fit: 150.8 GiB of weights per GPU), `--max-num-seqs 256`, `vllm bench serve` with 256 random prompts (6.2K input tokens on average), all succeeded. Every rank saved the same counts.

The other GEMMs got the same entries in both runs (22 buckets each).

`wq_b` is tuned with a bf16 input, while the forward passes a pre-quantized `QuantizedActivation`. Both reach the same `mm_mxfp8` call with the same shapes, and the forward hit the tuned entries: there was no warning during CUDA graph capture (M from 6 to 8190) or serving.

To reproduce: start the server with FlashInfer autotune on and grep the log for `No tuned config covers mxfp8_gemm input_shapes=((..., 1280), (1280, 4096)`, or check the saved `autotune_configs_*.json` for `(1280, 4096)` entries.

`pre-commit` passes on the changed files. CI does not run this path: it needs SM100 and the DSV4.1 checkpoint. I did not add a unit test, because it needs an MXFP8 `wq_b` on SM100 with FlashInfer.

## Details

The autotune dummy run spreads `max_num_batched_tokens` over up to `max_num_seqs` requests, so each one has only tens of tokens. The indexer then takes its short-context path (`max_seq_len // compress_ratio <= index_topk`) and returns before `wq_b`. CUDA graph capture does run `wq_b` (it skips that path), but capture only reads the autotune cache.

On main, a step that hits an untuned M falls back to `CuteDSLMxfp8GemmRunner` and compiles a kernel for that shape inside `execute_model`. In one run, while another server on the same node was compiling, that step went past `VLLM_EXECUTE_MODEL_TIMEOUT_SECONDS` (300 s). The engine died with a `TimeoutError` in the shm broadcast dequeue, right after logging the `(16376, 1280) x (1280, 4096)` fallback.

`_run_flashinfer_autotune_dummy_runs` now calls `autotune_indexer_wq_b` inside the same `autotune(tuning_buckets=..., round_up=True)` context as the dummy run. It runs every indexer's `wq_b` at the max tuning M with a random bf16 input. FlashInfer keys each config on the op, runner, input shapes and runner extras (output dtype and PDL for `CuteDSLMxfp8GemmRunner`), and skips profiling on a cache hit. So indexers that share a key are tuned once, and any indexer with a different dtype, quantization or backend gets its own entries. On DSV4.1-Flash the 8 indexers share one key, and the autotune pass did not get slower.

Alternatives considered:

- Skip the short-context path in the indexer forward while FlashInfer is tuning (the first version of this PR). It works, but it makes the forward read FlashInfer's global tuner state on every step.
- Give the autotune dummy run a long context (`_dummy_run(context_len=...)`). This changes the autotune pass for every model, exists only in MRV2, and gives every dummy request about `max_model_len` of context, far more than the KV pool can hold.

No other open PR tunes this GEMM.

commits.pr_title: [Perf][KV Offload] Keep offload event metadata out of the cyclic GC
commits.pr_body:
## Overview

`OffloadingEventsTracker` keeps one `_OffloadEventMetadata` entry for every chunk resident in any offload tier, and each entry held three objects tracked by Python's cyclic GC. With a large secondary tier, these entries make up most of the EngineCore's long-lived heap, so every full collection pauses the scheduler for over 100 ms. This PR keeps the entries out of the cyclic GC.

Not a duplicate. The only open PR touching this class is #63129 (draft). It fixes a separate correctness problem: metadata loss when an `OffloadKey` is reused. It doesn't change how entries are tracked.

## Claims

- Each event-metadata entry goes from 3 GC-tracked objects to 0.
- In a cold-cache KV-offload serving run, the full-collection pause drops from 106 to 31 ms and ITL p99 from 119 to 55 ms, and req/s rises 7%. That is within 1.5% of the same run with GC disabled.
- No behaviour change: residency bookkeeping keeps `set` semantics, and the emitted events are unchanged.

## Validation

| Cold-cache run | main | this PR | GC disabled (reference) |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| req/s | 13.5 | **14.5** | 14.7 |
| ITL p50 / p99 | 14.5 / 119 ms | 14.3 / **55 ms** | 13.9 / 49 ms |
| TTFT p50 | 2398 ms | 1803 ms | 1800 ms |
| Full-collection pause, mean / max | 106 / 121 ms | **31 / 38 ms** | – |
| Objects scanned by a full collection | 252,147 | **49,209** | – |
| ...of which event-metadata entries | 199,969 | 0 | – |

**Setup:**
- **Engine:** `vllm serve Qwen/Qwen3-0.6B --load-format dummy`, with `OffloadingConnector` + `TieringOffloadingSpec`: an 8 GiB CPU primary tier plus a KVCR secondary tier with 65,536 slots. KV events and `self_describing_kv_events` are on.
- **Mocks:** only the model forward and the GPU↔CPU copies are mocked, by a `UniProcExecutor` subclass passed via `--distributed-executor-backend`. A step is modeled as 10 ms plus 3 µs per prefill token. No GPU is used.
- **Load:** 64 concurrent unique 8K-token prompts, 128 output tokens.
- **Runs:** one 90 s window per arm, back to back, on `41f5146b5b`. There are no offload-path changes between that commit and this branch's base. The GC-disabled reference is a 30 s window.
- **Measurement:** pauses come from `gc.callbacks`, and object counts from `gc.get_objects()` at the end of the window. I can share the mock executor.

This change does not affect model outputs, so no model evaluation was run.

Tests:

```bash
pytest tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/offloading_connector/test_events.py \
  tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/offloading_connector/test_scheduler.py \
  tests/v1/kv_offload/tiering   # 1123 passed
pre-commit run --files <changed files>   # passed (ruff, mypy, ...)
```

`test_reoffload_preserves_secondary_residency` now also asserts that the entry is untracked, and checks through removals that both residencies survive a re-offload.

## Details

**Why each entry had three tracked objects:**
- the slotted dataclass, since dataclass instances are always tracked;
- the `active_residencies` `set`;
- one `(Medium, ownership)` tuple per secondary residency. `Medium` members are tracked objects, so the collector never untracks that tuple.

**The change:**
- `_OffloadEventMetadata` is now a `msgspec.Struct` with `gc=False`, the same pattern `KVCacheEvent` uses. Its fields are hashes, token ids, ints, strings and a shared `NamedTuple`, so an entry can't be part of a reference cycle.
- `active_residencies` is now an `int` bitmask. A `(medium, ownership)` pair gets the next bit the first time a store expects its removal. The table belongs to the tracker, survives `reset()`, and is bounded by the number of distinct tier/ownership pairs. A removal for a pair that was never registered clears nothing, as `set.discard` did.

`freeze_gc_heap()` doesn't help here, because it only freezes objects that exist at startup. The largest remaining source of scanned objects is the CPU tier's per-chunk `ChunkStatus`, which this PR leaves alone.
